highlights: TWO NEW KINDS OF CHIP JOIN THAT ROW: A WATCH ALERT THAT JUST FIRED, AND A BUFF THAT IS ABOUT TO RUN OUT. Both are things with a deadline and something to do about them, which is what earns a place on top of the game — and neither had one before. WHEN A WATCH RULE FIRES you already get a banner, and a banner is gone in six seconds whether or not you were looking at the widget. Now a chip with the rule's name and a bell also appears on the row and stays for THIRTY SECONDS, counting itself down, so you can look up from the fight and still find out what happened. Right-click it to dismiss it; the rule is untouched and the next match brings it straight back. This only happens for rules you have left "Banner alert on match" switched on for — a rule you deliberately silenced stays silent, and its sound and spoken alert are unchanged either way. WHEN A BUFF IS ABOUT TO FADE it gets a chip with an hourglass and the same countdown the Buffs card shows, "est" and all, with a gauge that empties as the time does. It uses the warning time YOU ALREADY SET — Options → Alerts & chips, the same number the Buffs card uses to decide what counts as expiring, sixty seconds unless you changed it — so there is no new setting to find and the card and the chip can never disagree. It clears itself when the buff fades or you get it recast. THE BUFFS CARD IS COMPLETELY UNCHANGED, and so is everything already on the chip row: mez and slow chips come first, then spawn countdowns, then alerts, then buffs. NOTHING NEW TO CONFIGURE: there are no new tick-boxes and no new sliders in this change. If you want a whole family of these off, that switch is coming — for now, a watch rule's own banner tick-box turns its chip off with it.

YOUR SPAWN CHIPS AND MEZ CHIPS ARE NOW ONE ROW UNDER THE WIDGET, AND IT FOLLOWS THE WIDGET WHEREVER YOU PUT IT. There used to be two separate floating stacks with two saved positions — spawn countdowns in one, mez and slow chips in the other. They are one horizontal row now, sitting just under EQBuddy (above it, if the widget is near the bottom of your screen), and it moves with the widget instead of being parked on its own. Mez and slow chips come first, then spawn countdowns. EVERYTHING A CHIP DOES IS UNCHANGED: a spawn chip still flips to DUE in warn red and a click clears it, a double-click still opens that zone's camp list, right-click still dismisses a spawn timer or a slow, the gauges still fill for spawns and drain for mez, and "Mez countdown chips" and "Track spawns" are still the switches in Options → Alerts & chips. The chip size slider is untouched. WHAT YOU LOSE, SAID PLAINLY: you can no longer DRAG the chips — they have no position of their own any more, which is the point of the change — and with the drag go the two "Spawn chips grow upward" and "Mez chips grow upward" tick-boxes and the empty "drag me — chips appear here" placeholder that used to show while Options was open. Wherever you had parked either stack is forgotten. WHY: two always-on-top stacks you had to place yourself, each of which could wander (that was discussions #122 and #152), is a chore the app should not be asking you to do — and one row that follows the widget is one thing to position instead of three. The row is on screen whenever there is a chip on it, whether EQBuddy is minimized or open, exactly as the two stacks were.

THE WORLD CARD IS NOW THE WORLD WINDOW — right-click the widget and choose “World…”, exactly as you already could. The card has left the widget, which now carries eight cards instead of nine; nothing about the World window itself changed. Its four tabs — Map, Camps, Path and Travels — are exactly as they were, the Travels tab still lists your deaths, the zones you have visited and your zone markers, and the “Show in mini dashboard” star for deaths lives there and always has. THERE ARE THREE WAYS IN: the “World…” row in the right-click menu, which is where it has been since the World fold and needed no change for this; the “Zone map” and “Spawn timers” hotkeys in Options → Hotkeys, if you have bound them; and the World room in the new EQBuddy window. If you had hidden the World card, or dragged it to a particular place in your stack, that setting is simply dropped — there is no row for it in Options → Cards & windows any more, because there is no card. WHAT YOU LOSE, SAID PLAINLY: the card's collapsed one-line summary — “Befallen · 2 zones · 1 death · 3 timers” — has no equivalent on the window's tab strip, which shows the zone and the death count but deliberately never a live timer count. And Options → Cards & windows no longer names Travels & Deaths, Zone map, Travel route or Spawn timers anywhere, because that note hangs under a card that is gone. WHY: the widget sits on top of the game, and a card whose whole job is to open a window is the clearest thing that does not need to be there — a map, a route and a camp list are things you look away for, not things you glance at mid-pull. This is the second card to move out this way, after Quests, and it went second for the same reason Quests went first: it strands nothing.

XP AND DPS/HPS ARE ALWAYS-ON HUD NUMBERS NOW, AND THEIR STARS ARE GONE. Minimize the widget and it always shows three things: your character name, your DPS, and your XP%/hr. You no longer switch those on — there is no ⭐ beside "Combat" or "Healing" any more, and no XP star in the Progress window, because there is nothing left to turn off. WHAT REPLACED THE TOGGLE: the third number swaps to HPS by itself whenever healing has been the weight of the last half-minute, and goes straight back to XP%/hr the moment you start dealing damage again — one number, swapped, not a second meter. Every other mini-dashboard star is exactly where it was: Kills, Pet damage, Weapon procs, Loot, Motes, Coin and Deaths still tick on and off in Options → Cards & windows and on their card headers, and anything you had starred there is untouched. THE DAMAGE AND HEALING POP-OUT WINDOWS ARE UNCHANGED and keep whatever state you had them in — they used to need the star AND the tick in Options → Cards & windows, and now the tick is the whole switch, so a window you had open stays open and one you had closed stays closed. The one gesture that moved: double-clicking the xp chip used to open the Progress window, and double-clicking the always-on XP number does exactly that now.

THE QUESTS CARD IS NOW THE QUEST TRACKER WINDOW — right-click the widget and choose “Quests…”. The card has left the widget, which now carries nine cards instead of ten; nothing about the Quest Tracker itself changed. Its four tabs — Quests, Epic 1.0, Plane of Sky and Unlocks — are exactly as they were, your checklists keep ticking themselves from your loot whether the window is open or not, and EQBuddy Mobile's Quests screen is untouched. THERE ARE THREE WAYS IN: the new “Quests…” row in the right-click menu, beside “World…”; the “Quest tracker” hotkey in Options → Hotkeys, if you have bound one; and the Quests room in the new EQBuddy window. If you had hidden the Quests card, or dragged it to a particular place in your stack, that setting is simply dropped — there is no row for it in Options → Cards & windows any more, because there is no card. WHY: the widget sits on top of the game, and a card whose whole job was to open a window is the clearest thing that does not need to be there — quests are something you read, not something you glance at mid-pull. This is the first card to move out this way, and it went first because it costs you nothing: it fed no star on the mini dashboard, so no number left the mini bar with it.

LEGACY LINUX/MACOS: YOUR 1.x BUILD KEEPS WORKING, AND IT STAYS DOWNLOADABLE. EQBuddy Evolved is Windows-only, and the Linux and macOS builds are NOT being taken down. The final cross-platform release is [v1.99.18](https://github.com/DranakCorps-bot/EQBuddy/releases/tag/v1.99.18), and that tag stays up permanently with its notes, its source and all three non-Windows downloads - EQBuddy-linux-x64.tar.gz, EQBuddy-osx-arm64.zip and EQBuddy-osx-x64.zip. A copy you already have goes on working exactly as it does today, with your settings, history and archives untouched: nothing is downloaded, staged, installed, removed or migrated off Windows, ever, and EQBuddy will never offer you a Windows installer that cannot run on your machine. Linux and macOS exist at all because Don Thompson built the cross-platform app and carried it through release after release of parity work, and quasarj contributed the macOS click-through, spoken alerts and Wine log-folder detection - thank you both; that work stays downloadable. The full support matrix, the download links and the promise in detail are in LEGACY-V1.md in the EQBuddy repository.

SOME OPTIONS LABELS NOW SAY “EQBuddy” WHERE THEY USED TO SAY “the widget” — same tabs, same order, same switches, nothing has moved. Look’s “Widget size” is now “EQBuddy size” and “Whole-widget opacity” is now “Overall opacity”; Behavior’s three “Hide the widget…” boxes now read “Hide EQBuddy…”, and several of the explanations under them are worded the same way. Every one of them does exactly what it did before and is in exactly the same place — the sliders, the theme picker, the grid overlay, the cursor ring, EQBuddy Mobile pairing, the hotkeys, the regen number, auto-empty and the rest. WHY: EQBuddy is growing a second, larger window, and these settings will be shown in both places out of one shared piece of the app rather than written out twice and left to drift apart. “Widget” was our word for the app rather than yours, so it goes now, while the change is a relabel and not a surprise later. ONE ACTUAL FIX RODE ALONG: the Behavior tab printed the log-archive explanation twice, one paragraph directly under the other. It says it once now.

Nothing is downloaded, staged, installed, removed or migrated off Windows, ever. The final Linux tarball and the macOS .app bundles stay on GitHub permanently, with their notes, tag and source. Linux and macOS exist at all because Don Thompson built the cross-platform app and carried it through release after release of parity work, and quasarj contributed the macOS click-through, spoken alerts and Wine log-folder detection - thank you both; that work stays downloadable. The full support matrix, the download links and the promise in detail are in LEGACY-V1.md in the EQBuddy repository.

FIXED (discussion #252, thanks TiconaX) - CARDS YOU HAVE HIDDEN NOW STAY HIDDEN. "The cards always reset to having 2 cards open even though I have hidden all of them. Gear & loot and + Motes." Your choice was being saved correctly every time; two old one-time upgrade steps had simply never stopped running, and each launch undid you. When the Motes card came back as its own card, the step that had folded it into Progress was never told - so it went on folding it away and un-hiding it, every launch. And a second step kept re-adding the old separate Gear card, which no longer exists, which made the Gear & Loot fold run again each time and un-hide that one too - and Progress with it, if you had hidden that as well. Both steps are finished and gone. Hide the cards once more and they will stay hidden. While this lasted EQBuddy was also rewriting your settings file on every launch; it no longer does.

FIXED - THE EQBUDDY MOBILE PAIRING LINK NOW USES YOUR WI-FI ADDRESS, AND YOU CAN PICK (discussion #264, thanks brhanson2-cyber - "the link it gives me is the ip address of my ethernet, not my wifi. How do I force it to give me a link using the wifi ip"). On a PC plugged into the router AND on Wi-Fi, both addresses looked identical to EQBuddy, so Windows' own ordering decided which one the QR carried - and it often chose the wired one, which your phone may not be able to reach. Wi-Fi now wins that tie, because the device scanning the code is on Wi-Fi by definition. And because no rule can know which network your phone is on, the pairing window now lists every address this PC has, right under the link, so you can point it at whichever one you want - it says which is the Wi-Fi one, and your choice is remembered. The list only appears if this PC actually has more than one address. Nothing else changed: virtual machine, WSL and VPN adapters are still kept out of the code, exactly as before. Windows, Linux and macOS alike.

FIXED - A BONUS XP WEEKEND IS COUNTED AGAIN (discussion #273, thanks brhanson2-cyber - "The bonus exp weekend has modified the xp message and eqbuddy is not registering any exp today"). During a bonus weekend the game writes "You gain experience (with a bonus)! (3.200%)", and EQBuddy recognised only the ordinary "You gain experience! (0.5%)" - so every XP hit of the weekend was read as nothing at all, and the Experience surfaces sat at zero while you played. Both wordings are now read, on solo and on party XP alike, and the percent is taken from the line exactly as it always was. Windows, Linux and macOS alike.

EQBUDDY MOBILE CAN NOW MAKE A SOUND WHEN AN ALERT FIRES (discussion #208, thanks sbaum23 - "As long as I can turn off alerts/chip in EQBuddy but leave them on in mobile (with the sounds for alerts happening in the browser) I think that will work for my use case"). Off until you turn it on, in Options - Behavior - Mobile sounds, beside the pairing button. With it on, a paired phone or tablet plays a tone whenever the PC raises a watch alert or a camp comes due - the same alerts and the same per-rule choices, so a muted rule stays muted on both. Your PC's own alert sounds are untouched and keep their own settings. One thing no setting can change: a browser will not play a sound until the page has been tapped once, so tap anywhere on EQBuddy Mobile after opening it - the Screens panel says whether this device is ready. Windows, Linux and macOS alike.
THE SKY TAB’S “OTHER CLASSES STILL WANT” HOVER NOW LEADS WITH “NOT YOURS”, SO THE PHONE STOPS CUTTING THE CAVEAT.

THE SKY TAB NOW CATCHES REWARDS YOU TURNED IN BEFORE EQBUDDY EXISTED, FROM YOUR OWN BAGS (discussion with Hateborne - "I *did* complete the Ivory Mask quest and have it in my bank... the 'Ready to turn in' box still shows it as ready to turn in"). The checklist tracks the INGREDIENTS a reward takes, and nothing had ever looked at the finished reward itself - so a turn-in done before EQBuddy existed sat "ready" forever, because a hand-in never appears in the log and the achievements dump cannot be trusted for a class unlocked at character creation (the game marks those rewards obtained without the items ever existing, and EQBuddy rightly refuses to believe it). Your bags are the witness that cannot lie: run /outputfile inventory and any open Sky reward whose finished item is in your bags or bank is marked turned in, with a report on the Sky tab naming exactly which ones and an Undo beside it - and right-click any reward to reopen it if EQBuddy has this wrong. The tab also now carries its own copy /outputfile inventory button beside the achievements one, the same pair the Unlocks tab has always shown, because this surface is fed by both dumps and only ever named one. Windows, Linux and macOS alike.

A READY SKY REWARD FOR A CLASS YOU HAVE ALREADY UNLOCKED NOW SAYS SO (Hateborne again - "I have unlocked the class AND I own the item"). Holding every piece of, say, the Necklace of Whispering Winds with Enchanter already unlocked is still worth a hand-in - the item is real - but the unlock it once bought is spent. The row now carries "ENC already unlocked - turn in for the item only", on both desktops and on EQBuddy Mobile's Ready band, so the list ranks what the errand actually gets you.

THE SKY TAB'S THREE SUMMARY BOXES NOW FOLD TO ONE LINE (Hateborne - "the first image shows how bloated it is"). "Ready to turn in", "No longer needed" and "Other classes still want" each carry a chevron: click the heading and the box collapses to a single line keeping its count, click again to expand. The folds last for the session and every launch starts expanded - the boxes are the tab's answers, so they must never be born hidden.

FIXED - "KEEP EQBUDDY OUT OF THE ALT+TAB SWITCHER" NOW ACTUALLY HIDES THE MAIN WIDGET (Hateborne - "It is enabled, but I can still Alt+Tab to it"). The option was doing its work on every window EXCEPT the one you could see: the style that leaves the switcher was set correctly everywhere, and on the main widget Windows overrides it for any window that owns a taskbar button. Turning the option on now also drops that button - which is the cost the tick-box's own warning has promised all along, and the tray icon remains the way back. Every satellite window behaved correctly throughout; it was only ever the widget itself that stayed.

YOUR LEVEL-UP TIMES ARE NOW IN PROGRESS > EXPERIENCE > LEVEL-UPS, AND THEY SURVIVE THE NIGHT (discussion #240, thanks joeymavity - "leveling timestamps in an xp dropdown, I can't find it now"). The only level times EQBuddy ever drew were on one line in the Experience summary, and that line is about the session you are in - so a fresh evening with no ding in it had nothing to show, which is exactly what happened to him. Beside that line there is now a Level-ups list holding every level-up EQBuddy has ever seen for that character: this session's and every archived one, merged into a single list, newest first, each with the day and time it happened. It starts FOLDED, because a long-standing character's list is a career rather than an evening - and the heading carries the count and the last one's date ("Level-ups (17) · last Aug 23"), so the glance answers "when did I last level" without opening anything. Click the heading for the rows; hover a row to see how long it had been since the level before it. Nothing was moved or removed to make room: the session line you already had is untouched, and Session History's level chart is exactly as it was. Windows, Linux and macOS alike - and EQBuddy Mobile's Experience tab folds the same list, from the same rows the PC drew, so the phone beside you answers it too.

THE SKY TAB NOW TELLS YOU WHICH SKY ITEMS YOU ARE DONE WITH (discussion #243, thanks tvongaza - "when you do an inventory dump, it could cross check which sky quests you've completed and which sky quest items you no longer need as you've completed all the quests which use them. Would help with limited inventory space."). EQBuddy already knew what Sky wants, what you have turned in, and what your bags hold; nothing had ever put the three together. Run /outputfile inventory and the Quest Tracker's Plane of Sky tab now carries two lists under "Ready to turn in", each row reading like "Azure Ring ×1 · bags" so you know where to go looking. The two lists are deliberately kept apart, because they are claims of different strength. "No longer needed" means every Sky reward in the game that takes that item is turned in - the strong claim, and the one you asked for. "Other classes still want" means it is still wanted, but by no class this character has: a Legends character can unlock one of those later, so it is "not yours" rather than "junk", and it will never be listed under the first heading. Hover any row for the evidence - which rewards used it, or which classes still want it. An item some OTHER quest in the catalog still takes is kept out of "no longer needed" and named underneath it instead ("1 more is still wanted by Blackburrow Brewers"), because the only way this feature could cost you anything is a wrong "safe to free". It lists, and nothing else: it ticks nothing, sells nothing and destroys nothing. Both lists are simply absent until you have run a dump and there is something to say. Windows, Linux and macOS alike - and EQBuddy Mobile's Plane of Sky tab now carries the same two lists, in the same words, off the same dump the PC read, so the phone propped beside you answers "can I free this" without you reaching back for the keyboard.

FIXED - AN ITEM IN YOUR SHARED BANK IS NO LONGER SHOWN AS GEAR YOU ARE WEARING. On the Gear tab, a row sitting in the shared bank was ranked as the most prominent location an item can be in and then labelled "worn · SharedBank1" - so the game's own dump said shared bank and EQBuddy said you had it equipped. Only the plain "Bank" spelling was ever recognised as a bank; the shared bank is one too, and both halves of the Gear tab now ask the same single question rather than each spelling the rule for themselves.

FIXED (discussion #253, thanks HiramDucky) - TURNING OFF "SHOW WATCH CHIPS IN THE MINI DASHBOARD" NOW STICKS. If any watch rule was pinned - and the built-in CC-broke rule is pinned out of the box, so this was most people - unticking that box in Options lasted exactly until you closed EQBuddy. Your choice was saved correctly every time; a one-time upgrade step that turned the group pin ON for anyone with a pinned rule had simply not been marked as one-time, so it ran again on every launch and undid you. It now runs once, on the upgrade it was written for, and never again. Nothing changes for anyone who wants the chips: if they are on today, they stay on.

SPELL HOVERS NOW READ THE SPELL'S OWN WIKI PAGE, AND 917 OF THEM SAY MORE THAN THEY DID. Hovering a spell in the level-up unlocks list used to show the one-line blurb from eqlwiki's class table - "Summon an Animation", "Cures strong diseases in 6 sec". eqlwiki reorganised those tables and dropped that blurb, so the text now comes from each spell's own page instead: "Animates a weapon and shield to attack your enemies. Consumes a tiny dagger when cast." It is still the wiki's own wording, never ours. This refresh also brings 10 new spells, retires 9 the wiki removed, and adds this week's new items to the built-in item catalog.

SKILL-UPS FOLD NOW, ON THE EXPERIENCE SURFACE. The Skill-ups list in the Progress window's Experience tab (and on the widget's Progress card, which draws the same view) has a click-to-fold heading like the AA ledger beside it. It starts OPEN, so nothing you can see today disappears - and folded, the heading keeps the count, so you never lose the fact that skills went up. Your choice is remembered.

SOL B'S KOBOLD KING NOW STARTS A SPAWN TIMER. It never did, and the reason was a name: eqlwiki titles him "Solusek kobold king" while the game kills "a kobold king", so the catalog and your log were never talking about the same creature. The catalog keeps the wiki's name - eqlwiki stays our tie-breaker - and now also carries the name the game actually uses. His respawn is still learned from your own kills rather than asserted: the zone's default clock applies until EQBuddy has watched enough cycles to say better.

FIXED (discussion #241, thanks DasGud) - QUEST TRACKER HAVE-COUNTS NOW MATCH YOUR BAGS. A turn-in item's have-count was a running log tally that could never see a hand-in, a sale, or anything you picked up off-log - so a Sky Test could keep showing items you had already handed in, or miss ones you got another way (DasGud's report: 4 Sphinx Claws and 1 Mithril Bands showing when he had none, 15 Wind Rune Izah instead of his 17). Running /outputfile inventory now trues every tracked count up to exactly what your bags and bank hold at that moment - present in the dump is its exact count, absent is zero, and any manual count you had typed in is superseded by the game's own answer. Nothing changes if you never run the command; your log-derived counts work exactly as before.

AND TURNING A SKY REWARD IN NOW ACTUALLY CONSUMES ITS ITEMS. The Sky tab's turn-in button ticked the checklist but never told the quest ledger the items were handed in, so a reward's have-count stayed inflated until your next inventory dump corrected it. The button now consumes the same way the Quests tab's own turn-in button always has - reopening a reward still leaves your item ticks alone, exactly as before.

AND THE QUEST TRACKER NOW SAYS WHERE ITS COUNTS COME FROM. A line above the turn-in list explains it in one sentence - after you scan bags, the count is your dump, then the log since - because a hand-in never appears in your log and there was no way to tell that from the numbers alone. There are two ways to correct a count by hand when the log cannot: the Mark as turned in button, or right-click a row to clear it.

FIXED (discussion #246, thanks jlcrisp) - BLACKBURROW BREWERS ASKS FOR THREE CASKS, NOT ONE. The quest takes 3 Blackburrow Casks and the catalog listed 1, so the tracker called it done two casks early. The wiki had it right the whole time: it gives the count in prose ("recovered three of these casks") rather than in its item list, and that is the one shape the weekly wiki harvest cannot read, so the entry fell back to a single cask. Corrected by hand and pinned with a test so a future harvest cannot quietly reset it.

THE ZONE MAP, SPAWN TIMERS AND TRAVEL ROUTE ARE NOW ONE WINDOW CALLED WORLD - and here is where each one went, by name. The gear menu's Zone map is now World > Map. Spawn timers is now World > Camps. Travel route is now World > Path. And the Travels & Deaths card is now the World card, with your deaths and zone history on World > Travels. Nothing was removed. Three ways back if you go looking: the gear menu carries a single World... entry, every card header's pop-out arrow still opens the window, and the World card's row in Options > Cards & windows still lists all four old names, so you can spot it by any of them.

WHY THIS FOLD, SAID PLAINLY. EQBuddy grew fast and gave nearly every request its own card or its own menu line - which is how four separate gear-menu entries for one subject (where am I, what spawns here, how do I get there) ended up scattered. Grouping them is an organizing pass: it makes a much better first hour for a new player, and if you have been here a while you mostly experience the disruption of things moving. That cost is real, and it is exactly why every move above is named with its old place as well as its new one.

DROP CAMP MARKER IS NOW PART OF THE WORLD WINDOW. It used to be its own gear-menu entry; it now lives in the World window's own chrome and works from any of its four tabs - so marking a camp no longer means leaving the map to go hunting through a menu.

YOUR PHONE GAINS A TRAVEL PANEL, AND CAMP MARKERS PIN ON ITS MAP. The route the desktop shows on World > Path now reaches your phone as its own panel, built from the same shared module the desktop reads so the two cannot drift apart. Dropping a camp marker now plants a pin on the phone's map as well. Switch it on the way you switch on any phone panel, with the gear icon on the phone page.

YOUR CARD KEPT ITS SLOT. The World card is the same card that used to be called Travels & Deaths - same position, same show/hide setting in Options > Cards & windows - so nothing about your saved layout had to change. One header control did move, so it gets its own line: the star that puts deaths on the mini dashboard is now inside the World window, on the Travels tab next to the deaths it counts. Whether you had it starred carried over untouched.

PLANE OF SKY: SHADOW KNIGHT REWARDS NOW IMPORT (PR #238, built and contributed by Hateborne - this and the next three highlights are his work). If you play a Shadow Knight, the achievements dump was being read but every one of your Sky rewards was silently skipped: the game spells the class "Shadowknight" and EQBuddy spelled it "Shadow Knight", and the comparison quietly matched nothing. The two spellings are now understood everywhere. Re-run /outputfile achievements and your rewards fill in. Turning a Sky reward in also marks its Sky Test quest complete on the Quests tab now, which it never did before - one fact, told the same way on both tabs - and the Sky tab itself carries a one-click copy of the achievements command that feeds it.

QUEST TRACKER: A NEW UNLOCKS TAB. Race and class unlocks, read from /outputfile achievements and the newly-supported /outputfile faction dump: how far along each race's factions are, which class unlocks want which Sky rewards, and an honest note when an unlock was handed to you (created as that race, or a token) rather than earned - a granted unlock's own checkmarks are not evidence, and the faction dump is what actually says where you stand. Both commands are one click to copy from the tab itself. Nothing here reads the game's memory: it is the game's own files, read when they change.

RESIZABLE WINDOWS, FINISHED PROPERLY. 1.99.11 gave every pop-out a grabbable edge; this release adds the part you can see - an accent bar along the bottom, the same hint the main widget shows, appearing exactly when a drag would work. Pop-outs also stop opening tall enough to fill the screen (the Quest Tracker on a tall monitor opened at over 1,800 pixels; it opens around 1,000 now and you can still drag it as tall as you like), and any window size that was recorded before dragging actually worked - a size nobody chose - is discarded once, so windows you never touched go back to fitting their contents. If you HAD dragged a window to a size you liked, you will need to set it once more; it sticks from then on.

NEW OPTION: KEEP EQBUDDY OUT OF ALT+TAB. Off by default, in Options > Behavior. One honest cost, stated where you tick it: Windows treats the switcher and the taskbar as one setting, so the taskbar button goes with it and the tray icon is how you get the widget back.

FIXED (discussion #239, thanks disberon) - THE EXPAND AND MINIMIZE BUTTONS STAY UNDER YOUR CURSOR. Hitting Expand on the mini dashboard used to leave your cursor over Settings or Start a new session, because the window grew to the right while its left edge stayed put - so clicking again out of habit did something you didn't ask for. The window now holds its RIGHT edge still when it changes size between the mini bar and the full widget, which keeps the two buttons aligned in both directions: click, click again, and you toggle - nothing else. How far off the old behaviour put you depended on how many stats you had starred on the mini bar, which is why it could feel occasional.

LINUX AND MACOS: THE PROGRESS CARD NOW EXPANDS IN PLACE, like it has on Windows since 1.99.5. Clicking the card used to open the Progress window; now the theme's tabs appear right there on the widget - Experience, Wealth, Faction, and the Raids glance - with the arrow on the header still opening the full window for your second monitor. Popping the window out collapses the card (never both at once), closing the window leaves the card collapsed rather than re-growing the widget, and the tab you were on in the window is the tab the card reopens on.

KILLS & DROPS AND GEAR & LOOT NOW EXPAND IN PLACE TOO - on Windows, Linux and macOS alike. Clicking either card used to open its window straight away; now the card expands right on the widget with its tabs: Kills with the per-creature rows and the farming block, Loot with its slices and sort. Two tabs deliberately show a one-line glance instead of a full body - Drops (it reads the wiki, which a card sitting over your game should never be doing) and Inventory (a long filterable list belongs in a window) - with the arrow on the header opening the full window either way. Same rules as the Progress card: pop the window out and the card collapses, close the window and the card stays collapsed, and the tab you were on comes back with you.

AND THE QUESTS CARD COMPLETES THE SET - every theme card expands in place now, on all three platforms. Clicking Quests used to open the Quest Tracker; expanding it now shows the four tabs and answers the question you opened it for in one line: how many quests are ready to turn in. The Epic and Plane of Sky tabs show one class's checklist right on the widget - read-only, capped, with '... and N more' when there is more - and the full working tracker with search, filters and ticking stays one arrow away. The Unlocks tab shows its progress fraction inline. This is the finish line of the reorganizing pass: fewer cards, nothing lost, and each card now answers on the widget what it used to make you open a window to learn.

WIKI PACK: YOUR WHOLE HISTORY COUNTS NOW, NOT JUST TONIGHT (discussion #217, thanks Frankthetankk - his ask, his reasoning, and his test cases). The pack refused to suggest a rarity label under 10 kills - that stays, it is what keeps a thin sample from becoming a confident wiki edit - but it used to start counting from zero every session, so three 4-kill evenings on the same named never added up to anything. The pack now pools every session stored in your history plus the one you are playing, across all your characters: twelve real kills are twelve kills. Money ranges, faction hits and con-derived levels pool the same way, the scope line at the top says exactly what was counted ("165 kills of 13 creatures across 3 sessions"), and nothing is counted twice. Drops by Creature deliberately keeps its live view - "is this camp worth it tonight" is a different question.

WIKI PACK: YOUR CAMPED RESPAWN TIMERS CAN NOW REACH EQLWIKI - CAREFULLY (from the spawn-timer discussions, thanks n3cr0nk1tt3n and Frankthetankk). When you camp a named properly - its own death starts the clock, you never leave the zone - EQBuddy now remembers each observed cycle. Once THREE cycles agree within 15%, and only then, the pack offers the timer for the creature's wiki page: a paste when the page has no respawn_time, or both numbers side by side when the wiki says something different (never a paste-over). One clean gap is never enough - kill-to-kill alone can't determine a respawn, which is exactly why the community asked for something better than a thread of guesses. Nothing publishes itself: you open the edit link, review, and save.

WIKI PACK: A RARE SPAWN YOU CONFIRMED IS NOW A CONTRIBUTION EVEN WHEN ITS LOOT ISN'T. When the game's own /consider calls a creature "a rare creature", that fact belongs on its wiki page - but if the page already listed every drop you saw, the pack had nothing to hang it on and silently dropped it, for exactly the creature most likely to be a known named. It gets its own row now ("rare spawn confirmed - rare on 2 of 7 /considers") with the same description-field paste as before: an addition, never a replacement, because EQBuddy can't read what the page's description already says. Nothing is claimed for a page EQBuddy couldn't read, and a page that turned out not to be the creature's is never offered the paste.

THE POP-OUT PROGRESS FLOAT IS NOW THE PROGRESS WINDOW - and that means it finally has tabs. Double-clicking the xp chip on the minimized bar used to open a small fixed panel that showed Experience and nothing else: no Wealth, no Faction, no Raids, and no way to reach them without going back to the widget. It now opens the same Progress window the card's arrow opens, with Experience, Wealth, Faction and Raids across the top and Experience selected first. The old float is gone rather than kept alongside - one Progress surface, not two, which is why the small one never grew the tabs the big one got.

MORE WINDOWS CAN BE RESIZED - AND THE ONES THAT ALREADY CLAIMED TO BE, NOW ACTUALLY ARE. Progress, Quests, Gear & Loot and Kills & Drops have been set resizable since 21 August and none of them could be dragged: EQBuddy draws its own window frames, so there was no edge for your mouse to grab. There is now, on all of them. Spawns, Travel routes, Session history, the Fight timeline, Zone knowledge and the session picker join them, and Spawns, Travel, Session history and the Fight timeline also remember the size next time they open.

AND A WINDOW YOU HAVE NOT DRAGGED NOW FITS ITS CONTENTS. The Progress window's Experience tab has been opening about 200 pixels tall and scrolling since 1.99.6 - it measured itself on its very first frame, before your log had been read, and kept that size forever. It measures when there is something to measure now, and only stops following your content at the moment you grab an edge and choose a size yourself. That size is then remembered; if you never drag it, nothing is remembered and it keeps fitting itself.

Two windows deliberately did NOT change, and it is worth saying which. Options already resizes by dragging its edge and fits its own height to your screen, so a second resize mechanism would fight the one it has. Item info grows on its own as the wiki answer arrives, so handing it a manual size is a decision we have not made - say so on GitHub if you want it. (The wiki pack window was already resizable and stays that way.)

FIXED (discussion #234, thanks atrzonkowski) - YOUR NAMED KILLS ARE BACK IN THE SESSION SUMMARY. Under a session in History, "Kills by creature" and "Mob farming" were quietly showing only your top 10 and top 8 creatures by kill count - and a named is, by definition, the one you killed once. So an evening in Guk with a dozen kinds of trash at ten-plus kills each pushed Ghoul Savant, Ghoul Sentinel, Frenzied Ghoul and Bloodthirsty Ghoul off the bottom of both lists, while the Encounters list below them still showed every one. Nothing was ever missing from your data; the summary was cutting it off. Both lists now show everything you killed.

And where a list still has a limit, it now says so - "... and 5 more items" rather than simply stopping. A trimmed list that looks complete is what made this take a bug report to find: there was no way to tell a short session from a truncated one. The nameds are the part of a session you actually remember, which makes them the worst possible rows to drop silently.

FIXED, AND IT IS THE MOST SERIOUS BUG EQBUDDY HAS SHIPPED (reported by StrIIker-TV on Reddit, thank you - this was a real loss and the report was right). Auto-empty could empty your logs BEFORE you were asked whether you wanted it to, and it could empty log files you had renamed and kept for yourself. Two separate faults, both fixed. If you have been bitten by this, read the next two paragraphs - your text is probably still on disk.

The first fault: the consent question was asked a second too late. The first page of the tour asks whether to keep your log files, and the startup sweep correctly waits for your answer. But a second cleanup runs on a timer, and that one was never told to wait - it ran about a second after launch and emptied your logs while the question was still on screen, before anyone could physically read it. So if you ticked "Keep my log files" and were emptied anyway, your tick was not ignored and you did nothing wrong. You were asked after the fact. Both cleanups now wait for your answer, on Windows, Linux and macOS.

The second fault: the cleanup could not tell your files from the game's. It emptied anything named eqlog_*.txt, which is the game's own naming AND the naming of every copy you keep beside it - so renaming a log to eqlog_yourname_yourserver_2026-08-01.txt to save it, which is the obvious way to keep your history, put it directly in the firing line. EQBuddy now only ever empties a file with the exact shape EverQuest Legends itself writes. Anything you dated, numbered or copied - any name carrying a character the game never writes, like a digit, dash, space, dot or bracket - is left alone permanently. One honest caveat: a rename that adds ONLY letters (eqlog_name_server_old.txt) is indistinguishable from a real log by its name alone and is still swept, so put a date or a number in the copies you keep. A server whose short name contains an underscore is still handled correctly.

IF THIS HAPPENED TO YOU, CHECK YOUR Logs\archive FOLDER FIRST. Since 1.84.0 EQBuddy copies a log's full contents there before emptying it, and that is on by default - so in almost every case the text is still on your disk, named eqlog_yourname_yourserver_ and the date and time the session ended. EQBuddy never deletes anything in that folder. If your archive folder is empty, archiving had been switched off in Options, and in that case the content is genuinely gone and I am sorry.

Auto-empty exists so logs do not grow to gigabytes, and it stays - but it is your data and the app now behaves that way: it asks first and waits for the answer, it keeps a copy unless you tell it not to, and it only ever touches the file the game is writing.

FIXED (discussion #235, thanks LeBigNasty) - A PREVIEW WITH NOTHING TO APPLY NO LONGER LOOKS LIKE A BROKEN BUTTON. Import achievements reads your dump, shows what it found, and greys out Apply when every reward it recognized is already ticked. That is the right behaviour and it read as a dead button: the sentence explaining it sat at the top, above a list that can run to seventy rows, and the grey "Apply (0)" at the bottom is what you actually see. The button now says "Nothing to apply", a line beside it says your import worked and how many rewards were already marked, and hovering it explains the same thing. Nothing about how the import works has changed - only what it tells you.

YOUR CLASSES STAY ON SCREEN WHEN YOU USE THE CLASS PICKER. 1.99.7 started naming which classes you are and where that came from - and then hid the line the moment you ticked anything in the Quest Tracker's picker, which is exactly when you want to see it. Your classes are who your character IS; the picker is a lens you look through. The line stays now: "Warrior · Druid · Monk (from your achievements)" on the phone, the Quest Tracker and the buff-set editor, picked or not.

And it no longer tells you to "override" them. That word was wrong twice over: the picker widens what EQBuddy knows about you rather than replacing it, and being told to override your own character is a strange thing for an app to say. The line names where your classes came from and stops there. "Your picks" also reads "from your picks" now, so the three answers line up and you can tell a fact from a guess at a glance.

FIXED - the buff-set breakout called your classes a guess even when the game had told us. Its subtitle always said "inferred from your log", so a character whose classes came from an achievements dump was labelled as though EQBuddy had worked them out from what you cast. It says which of the three it actually was.

FIXED - EQBUDDY NOW KNOWS YOU ARE MORE THAN ONE CLASS. EverQuest Legends lets you be up to three classes at once, and EQBuddy did not believe it: everything class-aware - the quest filters, the Gear Locker, the Sky lens, the next-level spell list, the phone - was built on a single answer, and when two classes had comparable evidence it gave up and said it did not know. So a correctly-played Warrior/Druid/Monk was read as an ambiguous log rather than as a character, and the surfaces downstream showed nothing. If you have ever ticked classes by hand to make a list work, that is the reason.

And every surface now says WHERE your classes came from, because the three answers are not equally certain. "Warrior · Druid · Monk (from your achievements)" is the game's own word for it; "(inferred from your log)" is EQBuddy reading what you cast; "(your picks)" is the filter you set. The Quest Tracker, the buff-set editor, Options and the phone all use the same words, and the phone's quest screen now lists every class rather than one.

It now reads your ACHIEVEMENTS DUMP first, which is the game's own word for it. Your class-unlock achievements name every class you hold, and EQBuddy has been reading those rows for two releases - only to avoid ticking Sky rewards you were granted rather than earned. It reads them for what they say now, so if you have ever run /outputfile achievements (or let EQBuddy pick one up by itself), your classes come from the game rather than from a guess. A class you unlocked with a token counts: you are that class however you got there.

Where there is no dump, the log itself now names every class it can see instead of only the strongest. It still takes real evidence - three sightings and either a class-defining ability or two distinct class spells - so one borrowed clicky still names nobody. What changed is that a second class no longer cancels the first out. And the Quest Tracker's class picker goes back to being what it was meant to be: a filter you can widen to help a friend, never the thing that tells EQBuddy what your character is.

NEW - HOVER A SPELL IN PROGRESS AND IT TELLS YOU WHAT IT DOES. The next-level list and the ding list have always named the spells you are about to get and left you to look them up; the AA rows beside them have shown the wiki's own effect text for months, which is what made the silence on the spell rows look like an oversight rather than a decision. Hovering now gives eqlwiki's own one-line description - "Imbues your target with life after 0:00:18, healing for 5000." - followed by which of your classes gets it and when. The words are the wiki's, carried across exactly as written; EQBuddy does not compose them and never guesses at an effect.

AND THE SPELL LIST ITSELF IS RE-SOURCED FROM EQL WIKI'S CLASS PAGES. It was built from individual SPELL pages, which name every class that has ever had a spell across every version of EverQuest - wider than this game. The class pages are curated for Legends, so those are what EQBuddy reads now. Two things change on screen. Spells you were shown but never actually get at that level are gone - a druid's Level 34 list drops six Velious-era ports it was never going to grant you. And a spell that was missing entirely is back: Healing Water at Druid 34, which fell out because its wiki page carries another spell's name in one of its fields and our old import de-duplicated it away.

Levels 51 to 60 are marked, because the class pages stop at 50. Every class page on the wiki ends at level 50 while Legends goes to 60, and a few have gaps in the middle. Those levels are still answered - from the spell pages, as before - but the row now says "from its spell page" so you can tell a curated answer from a derived one at a glance. Nothing is hidden from you and nothing is quietly padded; if a level's information is thinner, it says so.

WHERE THINGS MOVED, AND WHY THEY KEEP MOVING (discussion #233, thanks mjtrainor - "stop changing every feature and it's location every release... I don't want to need to hunt for 'missing' features every single time I sit down to play EQL"). That is fair, and it has now been said three times - #219 lost the mote rate, #227 and #228 lost the Motes card. So here is the whole map in one place, and a promise about what happens next.

What has been going on: EQBuddy grew fast, one feature request at a time, and every one of them arrived as its own card on the widget. That is how you end up with fourteen cards and no idea which one holds the thing you want. The 1.98 and 1.99 releases are the ORGANIZING pass - putting things where they logically belong now that we know what they all are. The new homes should make more sense on their own terms, and they are far easier for somebody opening EQBuddy for the first time. But if you have been here a while, none of that is what you feel: what you feel is that something you knew the location of is somewhere else. Both are true, and the second one is the cost of the first.

The map, as of this release. PROGRESS is one card with four rooms - Experience (xp, AAs, skill-ups, what your next level unlocks), Wealth (coin), Faction, and Raids. It absorbed the old Progress, Money, Motes, Faction and Raids cards. GEAR & LOOT is one card with four tabs - Loot, Items, Wishlist and Inventory - and absorbed the Loot and Gear cards, with the old Gear Locker and Inventory windows now both living on the Inventory tab. KILLS & DROPS is one card with two tabs, Kills and Drops, and absorbed the Kills card and the Drops by Creature window. QUESTS has General, Epic and Sky. MOTES is its own card again if you want it - it is switched on in (gear) - Cards & windows.

Nothing was deleted in any of that, and there are three ways back to anything. Every folded card can be switched on again in (gear) - Cards & windows. Every card keeps the slot you dragged it to, so a merged card sits where its parts sat. And the arrow on any card header pops that surface out to a full window on a second monitor.

THE PROMISE, starting now: any release that MOVES a surface will say so in this list, by name, in the form "X is now Y" - the old place and the new one, not just the new one. You should never have to hunt for something EQBuddy relocated, and if you do, that is a bug in this list rather than something to go looking for. The organizing pass is also finite - it is nearly done, not a permanent state of affairs.

NEW - THE NEXT LEVEL'S SPELLS AND ABILITIES ARE SPLIT UP BY CLASS. Progress has always been able to tell you what your next milestone level opens up; now, on a character with more than one class, each class gets its own heading you can fold open or shut. A Legends character is up to three classes at once, so "what do I get at 34" was never one list - it was three, run together, and the only way to tell whose row was whose was to read the right-hand column of every line. The first class with something in it starts open and the rest start folded; that choice lasts the session and is deliberately not saved, because folding Warrior away to read Druid is a decision about the next thirty seconds. One class still gets its names straight under the heading, with no lone expander to click.

A class that gains NOTHING at that level keeps its row and says so. Warriors, Monks and Berserkers have no spell table at any level, so "Warrior - nothing new at 13" is the complete answer rather than a gap; dropping the heading would look exactly like that class not being one of yours. Abilities the wiki lists for everyone - General, Archetype and Special AAs - sit in their own "Any class" group instead of being repeated under each of your three, and a spell two of your classes both learn appears under both, because it really is two answers to the same question. The window, the widget and the phone all draw the same groups from the same place, so they cannot drift apart.

And the preview now stays hidden until EQBuddy actually knows a class for you, which is a change in what it will claim. Before this it would fall back to the abilities that apply to everyone and then jump forward to whatever level had one - so a character with no class picked could be told "at level 39: 1 new AA ability" about a pet ability, five levels away, with no pet. A forecast that cannot be about you should not say it is. If your classes are not showing, tick them in the Quest Tracker's class picker.

NEW - MOTES PER HOUR, AS ONE LINE ON PROGRESS. It sits in the Experience room with the xp and AA rates - "1 mote - 0.9/hr" - because that is the room open while you are actually at the camp. The Motes card keeps its own surface for anyone specifically farming them, and the Wealth pill stays coin; this is a summary of that card, in the place you were already looking, not a replacement for it. It is the same line the Motes card's own header shows, so the two can never disagree, and it stays off the screen entirely on a session where no motes have dropped rather than reporting a rate of nothing.

Small, on EQBuddy Mobile: the phone stops being woken by the mote rate ticking over. Its Progress screen used the rate as its way of noticing a mote had dropped, and a rate moves on the clock even when nothing happens - so a paired phone could wake for a number changing by itself. It watches the motes themselves now.

NEW - PLANE OF SKY STEPS ARE GROUPED BY ISLAND. A quest's pieces used to be one flat list that jumped from island to island; now the steps for an island sit together under its own heading, in island order, so you can see the work for where you are actually standing. Island 1.5 sorts where it belongs. Steps that drop from trash anywhere on the plane - Wind Runes and the like - keep the ungrouped listing they have always had, under "Anywhere on the plane", because "no island" is the true answer for those rather than a gap. Thanks to the Reddit player who suggested it.

Some Sky pieces drop on several islands at once, and there is a tick-box on the Sky tab for how you would rather see those. Off (the default) lists each one once, under a heading that names them - "Islands 1.5 · 4 · 8" - so you can see from where you are standing whether it is reachable. On repeats it under every island it drops on, so a single island's list is complete when you are planning a trip there - the same step then shows up more than once, which is the trade. Either way the score counts each step once, and the setting follows you to the phone.

FIXED (discussion #109, thanks Frankthetankk) - THE FIRST TWO BEES ON ISLAND 6 STOP GETTING RESPAWN COUNTDOWNS THEY DO NOT DESERVE. The Plane of Sky bee chain is four links - Bzzazzt, then Bazzzazzt, then Bzzzt, then Bazzt Zzzt - and EQBuddy only knew the last two. So the first two fell through to the zone's eight-hour default and started clocks, and because more than one wasp answers to each of those names - three Bzzazzt stand on the island at the start, and the Bazzzazzt they spawn share a name too - a gap between two of them could also be LEARNED as a respawn: kill two Bzzazzt three minutes apart and you had a three-minute timer that went DUE forever. Both are in the catalog now, along with Bizazzzt on the dead-end branch off the first pair, all marked as several-creatures-share-this-name so nothing is learned from them, and a wrong value already saved in your file is cleared the next time EQBuddy starts. Your own typed duration is never touched.

One of those two is NOT triggered, and it is worth saying why we went the other way on it. Frankthetankk asked for both to be marked triggered, and eqlwiki gives Bzzazzt a real 12-hour respawn - it is the mob that STARTS the chain, and a chain whose first link only appears when something else dies could never begin. His testing is all from personal Sky instances, which do not respawn once cleared, so a 12-hour open-world clock is invisible from there. Both accounts are true about different places; the catalog describes the world, and eqlwiki is what we match when the two disagree.

FIXED (discussion #101, thanks Frankthetankk) - WHEN EQBUDDY READS YOUR ACHIEVEMENTS DUMP BY ITSELF, IT NOW TELLS YOU WHAT IT DID. Since 1.98.1 EQBuddy has noticed the moment the game announces an /outputfile achievements dump and read it for you - marking Sky rewards you had turned in and raid clears from before EQBuddy. It did all of that silently: no report, no Undo, and no mention of anything it had skipped. The Raids surface now carries the same line the inventory dump has always shown on the Gear tab, with an Undo that puts back exactly what the import ticked and leaves anything you ticked yourself alone.

And it says what it did NOT do, which is the half that was costing you. Rewards from a class unlock you were GRANTED rather than earned are deliberately skipped - your primary class unlock is complete from character creation and the game flags its rewards as obtained without the items ever existing, so importing them would tick off Sky pieces you never had. That guard has been there since #101 and it was working; it just said nothing, so a dump full of rewards could report "nothing new to mark" and look broken. It now names the count. So does the other one: a reward the dump says you obtained whose name does not match anything on the checklist is counted too, because that one is real progress not being recorded, and only the manual Import achievements preview ever listed them.

Frankthetankk asked directly whether the automatic path skips the check that the manual menu makes. It does not - both go through the same guard, and there is now a test that says so rather than it being true by coincidence.

NEW (discussion #217, thanks Frankthetankk) - WHEN THE GAME ITSELF CALLS A CREATURE RARE, THE WIKI PACK OFFERS THAT AS AN EDIT. /consider prints "a rare creature" for a rare spawn, and that is a fact about the creature that eqlwiki has no systematic way to record yet. If your own con said it, the pack now hands you a line for the creature's page - "Confirmed as a rare spawn via in-game /consider" - alongside the drops it was already offering. Frankthetankk took the destination question to the wiki admins himself: there is no rare-spawn field on the creature template yet, they are positive about adding one, and until it lands the description field is the stopgap that matches what editors already do by hand. The pack says all of that, so nobody is left guessing why the line goes where it goes.

It is careful in three ways, and each one is a thing it refuses to do. It never tells you to replace what an editor has already written - EQBuddy cannot read the description field, so the only honest instruction is to ADD. It is never inferred from how often something drops or how rarely you find it: the only evidence is the game's own word in your own log, and a creature you never conned gets no line at all, because "I conned it and it never said rare" and "I never conned it" are different things. And it always shows both numbers - "on 2 of your 7 /considers" rather than just "rare" - because same-named spawns are not all rare and you are the one pasting it.

Creature rarity and item rarity stay completely separate, which is the part that was nearly got wrong. A trash mob can drop an ultra-rare item and a rare spawn can drop its piece every single time. The drop-rate labels still need 10+ kills and the wiki's own bands; this needs one /consider, because the game printed the word rather than us measuring anything.

The wiki contribution pack no longer offers to add MOTES to a creature's page (thanks Frankthetankk, #217, and LeBigNasty, #226). Motes drop from everything, so listing one under a creature's known loot is not a small edit to argue about - it is wrong, and wrong on every page you paste it onto. The wiki's own Mote Guide is the authority there. This is only about what gets suggested to the wiki: your motes still show everywhere EQBuddy shows loot, and ordinary common drops are still suggested, because the wiki admins asked for those to stay in.

FIXED - PETS ARE NO LONGER TRACKED AS NAMED MOBS ON SPAWN TIMERS. A named mob's pet has no "a" or "an" in front of it and starts with a capital, exactly like the named itself, so "Xanthus`s pet" was being learned as a spawn and given a respawn clock - for something that has no spawn cycle at all, only a summoner. A timer that will never come due teaches you to walk to a camp that isn't up. Any name ending in "pet" is now read as a pet, and EQBuddy quietly clears the ones your profile already learned the next time it starts. Names that merely contain the letters (Petrifier, Petras) are untouched.

The wiki contribution pack stops calling a wrong-article session "nothing to contribute". If every creature you looked up landed on a lore page rather than a creature page, the pack said there was nothing to add - which is EQBuddy having read the wrong page, not the wiki being complete. It now says how many pages weren't the creature, and the heading tooltip tells you what to do about it.

FIXED ON LINUX AND MACOS - CLOSING A THEME WINDOW AND OPENING IT AGAIN COULD BRING THE WHOLE APP DOWN. Progress, Gear & Loot and Kills & Drops all borrow one copy of what they draw from the widget, and a window that had been closed was still holding its copy - so the second time you opened one, it tried to draw something another window still owned and threw. Two clicks, every time, on all three windows, since the day they shipped. They let go of what they are holding when they close now. Windows was never affected.

FIXED (discussions #228 and #227, thanks daetien-lab and typical-usual-chaos) - IF YOU WERE WATCHING MOTES, THE MOTES CARD COMES BACK ON BY ITSELF. It returned as its own card in 1.99.0, but it returned switched OFF for everybody - so if motes vanished on you when they were folded into Progress, the fix handed them back with the light still out and you had no reason to go looking. EQBuddy now turns the card on for anyone who had motes on the minimised dashboard, once, on the next launch. It does this once - if you would rather not see it, switch it off again and it stays off.

FIXED (discussion #226, thanks LeBigNasty) - WHEN THE WIKI ANSWERS WITH THE WRONG ARTICLE, EQBUDDY SAYS SO INSTEAD OF CALLING IT AN EMPTY PAGE. His example is Innoruk, where the lookup lands on the Lore article rather than the creature's page. A lore article and a creature page nobody has filled in both come back with no loot on them, and EQBuddy could not tell them apart - so it read the god of hate as a creature whose drops were all news, and the contribution pack would have offered you a loot table to paste onto it. Drops by Creature now reads "that wiki page isn't the creature", and the pack lists it as something to look at rather than something to submit.

Being honest about the limit: turning it back on needs proof you cared about motes, and the only proof that survived the fold is that mini-dashboard star - when Motes became a tab in Progress, the record of whether you had the card showing was thrown away. If you watched the card without ever starring the stat there is nothing left to go on, so it stays hidden and (gear) - Cards & windows is still the switch. Showing it to everyone instead would grow a card on the widget of every player who never asked for one, which is the complaint this started as.

The Wealth tab no longer claims a mote rate it does not show. Its pill read "5p 1g 4s 8c - 1 mote - 0.9/hr" while the tab underneath is coin, and #227 settled that Wealth is coin and the Motes card owns the rate. The pill is coin now, on both the Progress window and the widget. Motes per hour is still on the Progress card's own line and on the Motes card, which are the two places that were asked for.

WINDOWS ONLY FOR NOW - THE PROGRESS CARD OPENS ON THE WIDGET INSTEAD OF SENDING YOU TO A WINDOW (thanks daetien-lab, #228: "I simply want to track my mote drops in the main window"). Click it and it unfolds in place with a row of tabs - Experience, Wealth, Faction, Raids - and the arrow on its header still pops the full window out to a second monitor, which collapses the card so the same surface is never in two places. The Linux and macOS widget still opens the window; the reason is an Avalonia bug we do not control, and it is next on the list.

Small: the Experience room stops drawing a "Skill-ups" heading on sessions where you did not raise a skill. It was always there with nothing under it, which reads as a list that failed to load rather than a session that had none.

FIXED (pull request #231, thanks quasarj) - LETTERS NO LONGER DRIFT APART IN THE MIDDLE OF WORDS UNDER WINE AND CROSSOVER. Text came out reading "an d th is" and "bun dles" - gaps of a pixel or two opening inside words. Nothing was wrong with the font: the letters were positioned correctly and then drawn in the wrong places. Windows places each letter with fractional precision; Wine drops the fraction instead of carrying it, so the error builds across a line and appears all at once as a gap. EQBuddy now asks for whole-pixel letter positions when - and only when - it is running under Wine. Windows is untouched.

AND YOU CAN TURN THAT OFF IF YOU RUN THE WIDGET LARGE. Options - Look has "Keep letters on whole pixels", and it only appears on Wine or CrossOver because it is the only place it means anything. Whole-pixel letters are lined up before the widget is scaled, so above 100% the text softens; if you would rather have sharp text than perfect spacing, untick it. No restart.

FIXED (pull request #231, thanks quasarj) - BOLD TEXT UNDER WINE AND CROSSOVER IS PROPERLY SPACED AGAIN, and the small-caps headings are back. EQBuddy bundles its own font for Wine, because Wine ships none of the Windows ones - and it was bundling only the plain weight. Asked for bold with no bold to give, Windows fakes one by thickening the plain letters where they stand, which widens every letter without moving the next one along. That is most of the numbers, every card heading and every stat value. The real semi-bold and bold now ship, and so do the small-capital letters that headings like "dps" and "kills" are drawn with.

Zone-knowledge imports no longer try to put a respawn clock on a raid-instance boss or a triggered spawn, and the preview says why instead of calling it a risky number. Before, those rows read "no local baseline to corroborate" under a checkbox offering to apply them anyway - and ticking it did nothing for them.

FIXED (discussion #226, thanks LeBigNasty and Frankthetankk, and #65 where it was first asked for) - THE DROPS TAB CAN RE-READ A CREATURE'S WIKI PAGE ON DEMAND, AND SAYS HOW OLD ITS LAST READ IS. FIXED (discussion #222, thanks bjstrange) - PULL-DOWN REFRESH WORKS ON EQBUDDY MOBILE WITH ONLY ONE CARD SELECTED. It asks your PC for fresh numbers rather than reloading the whole page, so your place on the page - and the map's pan and zoom - survive it; if the connection has dropped it reloads instead, because then that is the only thing that helps. FIXED (discussion #228, thanks joeymavity) - MEZ TIMERS STOP SWINGING BETWEEN TWO VALUES. If you cast a high rank, a mez broken early by damage could be mistaken for a measurement of how long that rank lasts, and overwrite the real duration EQBuddy had already watched you measure - so chips flipped between a short wrong number and the right one with nothing to explain either. EQBuddy checks: it takes a LONGER reading straight away, because an upgraded rank should not have to argue, but wants to see a SHORTER one twice before believing it, because two identical early breaks are far less likely than one. The trade is that a timer inflated by chain-mezzing now takes two clean casts to correct itself instead of one. And you can always type the duration yourself under Options - Alerts & chips, where your number wins outright.

FIXED - EQBUDDY MOBILE NOW USES YOUR DESKTOP THEME. It never has. Nothing looked broken - the page still had colours, just not yours - which is why nobody reported it. It had logged 563 times on one machine before anyone read the file. FIXED - EQBUDDY MOBILE NO LONGER GIVES UP WHEN WINDOWS WON'T GIVE IT THE PORT. Ticking Enable could produce "Couldn't listen on port 47998 - only one usage of each socket address is normally permitted" and stop there, on a machine where nothing was using that port at all: no program, nothing in any connection list, nothing reserved. Some drivers and VPN or virtual-machine networking hold ports at a level Windows does not show you. It now asks Windows for a port it WILL give, remembers it, and tells you which one it used. The pairing code carries the port, so there is nothing for you to change.

And the advice that used to come with that error - "change the port and try again" - has gone, because there was never anywhere to change it. That was the same defect as telling you to import a file without saying how.

FIXED - THE QUESTS SCREEN ON EQBUDDY MOBILE COULD GET STUCK ON "Waiting for the quest catalog from the PC..." FOREVER (thanks David, who found it on his phone within minutes of the last build). YOUR /OUTPUTFILE DUMPS NOW IMPORT THEMSELVES. Type /outputfile inventory in game and EQBuddy reads the file within a second or two - no menu, no Import button, no hunting through the game folder for a file you didn't know the name of. It works because the game already announces every dump it writes, by name, in the same log EQBuddy has been reading all along; nothing was listening to that line until now. Same for /outputfile achievements, which marks your raid clears and Sky rewards from before EQBuddy.

It TELLS you what it did - "Read your inventory dump (18:47) - 3 items ticked" - with an Undo beside it, because a change you didn't watch happen should be reversible. The Undo puts back only what the import ticked; anything you ticked yourself is left alone, and a witnessed raid kill is never taken away. It says the dump was read even when nothing changed, so "EQBuddy did nothing" and "EQBuddy never saw my file" stop looking identical.

GEAR & LOOT OPENS LANDSCAPE INSTEAD OF PORTRAIT, and the wishlist tab is called "Wishlist" instead of "Gear". THE GEAR TAB NOW HANDS YOU THE COMMAND INSTEAD OF JUST NAMING IT. It used to say "Import an EQ Legends Tools shopping-list HTML in Options" and stop there - a job with no directions and no tool. There's now a one-click copy of /outputfile inventory right on the tab, on the full list as well as the empty one, because the person most likely to need a fresh dump is the one whose import has gone stale.

And the empty tab explains what a gear list actually IS - a wishlist you build on the eqlegends.tools website and export - instead of saying "shopping list" as though everyone already knew. It used to name two completely unrelated imports in two sentences side by side, which read as one set of instructions and sent at least one person into Options looking for somewhere to feed a file that imports itself.

EQBUDDY MOBILE SHOWS THE COMMAND AS TAP-TO-SELECT TEXT rather than a copy button, on the Gear checklist and on Raids. A copy button on the phone would put the command on the phone's clipboard, which cannot reach the game running on your PC - so the phone tells you what to type and where to type it instead of offering a button that does nothing useful.

GEAR LOCKER AND INVENTORY ARE ONE TAB NOW, called Inventory, with a "Group by bag" switch. They always read the same file - the /outputfile inventory dump - so two separate windows off one dump just made you guess which was the real one. Off, it ranks everything wearable you own within each slot and marks what's an upgrade over what you're wearing and what's outclassed by something else in your bags. FIXED (discussion #202, thanks bjstrange) - EQBUDDY MOBILE'S LOOT CARD STOPS REBUILDING ITSELF. It had been flickering several times a second for three releases, and two confident fixes from here missed it, because the page was not at fault: the PC was sending it two DIFFERENT versions of the loot card, twenty times a second one way and once a second the other. EQBuddy pushes to a paired device from two places - a fast path for low latency and the normal one-second refresh - and the fast path was building its numbers without your watch rules, so every push said the watch list had emptied and every refresh said it had refilled. The phone was doing exactly the right thing with what it was told. Both paths now build the same numbers, which also makes the fast path free instead of rebuilding everything twenty times a second. bjstrange's two debug screenshots, nine seconds apart and exact mirror images, are what finally showed it.

Ticking one now turns it on properly - it stars the stat for you - and the box shows whether the window would actually open rather than only whether you had dismissed it, so a row you never set up now reads as off instead of pretending to be on. YOU CAN NOW TYPE YOUR OWN MEZ DURATIONS (asked on Reddit). Each row says where its current number came from - what you typed, what EQBuddy measured from your own casts wearing off, or what is documented - so you can see what you are overriding. Clear a box to hand the spell back; EQBuddy keeps measuring in the background the whole time a typed value is in place, so clearing it lands on what has been seen SINCE rather than on whatever it knew that day. Before this, a mez timer that had learned something wrong could only be fixed by deleting a file by hand.

SPAWN TIMERS NO LONGER LEARN A RESPAWN YOU DID NOT WATCH (David). If you leave the zone while a countdown is running, the gap to your next kill no longer teaches EQBuddy anything. That covers an ordinary evening that used to poison a timer outright: log out beside a camp, log back in at D0 where the named is up, kill it, then change to your own instance and run to the spawn point - where it is up as well, because that is a different copy of the zone. Killing it there looked like a twelve-minute respawn. It also drops the "killed it, went to sell, came back an hour later" gaps, which were true and useless. Your countdown itself is untouched and keeps running while you are away - the named goes on respawning, and your instance keeps its state.

SPAWN TIMERS: NAMED WITH NO LISTED RESPAWN NOW LEARN THEIR OWN. 126 named ship in the catalog with the respawn field blank, in zones that have no fallback either - every one of the 38 in High Keep (Princess Lenia among them) and 47 in Western Wastes. Those were worse off than a mob EQBuddy had never heard of: an unlisted named measures its cycle from your second kill, while these could never learn one at all. Kill one twice in a sitting and it now has a countdown, and it keeps tightening as you camp.

SPAWN TIMERS: the Spawns window can finally tell you WHERE a timer came from - your own kills, seeing the named up before its clock ran out, or someone else's shared zone knowledge. Imported timers used to be indistinguishable from your own the moment they landed, and the tooltip admitted it ("your kills or an import") because the app had not kept the fact. Your own kills replace an imported number, and a duration you type still outranks all of them.

Update the PC and the two halves would quietly disagree while reporting the same version number. THE QUEST TRACKER HAS BEEN REBUILT AROUND A LIST AND A DETAIL PANE. The left column is now one compact row per quest: its name, a state badge (ready / a progress count / open / done), and one line of zone, giver, level and how many zones away it is. Pick one and the right-hand pane shows everything that used to be crammed into the card - the rewards, the turn-ins with their counts, and a labelled Zone / Giver / Level / Distance / Class strip that no longer quietly loses the class off the end of a line.

A green rule runs down the edge of a row whose turn-ins are all in hand, an amber one down a row you've started, and a line above the list says "8 quests ready to turn in" before you've looked at a single row. If nothing is ready it says nothing at all rather than "0 quests ready", which read as a broken tracker.

AND HANDING A QUEST IN IS A BUTTON NOW. Marking a turn-in used to be a click on the progress COUNT - an affordance whose only signal was a tooltip nobody hovers. The detail pane has a proper "Mark as turned in" button, and track / mark-done / hide / report-bad-data are real buttons beside the quest name instead of five tiny glyphs repeated on every card.

A QUEST FINISHED BEFORE THAT YOU CAN DO AGAIN NOW READS "READY", NOT "DONE". Repeatable quests with a full set of turn-ins in your bags were being labelled by their history rather than by what you're holding.

REWARDS SHOW WHAT KIND OF THING THEY ARE. Each reward carries a small silhouette worked out from the item's own stats - a sword, a mace, a bow, a shield, a helm, a ring, a cloak, a crate for everything else - so a list of eight rewards can be skimmed. Weapons follow their SKILL rather than their slot, so a two-handed blunt is drawn as a mace and not a sword. Hovering still pulls the item's live wiki stats, and clicking still opens its page.

EVERY ICON IN THE TRACKER IS NOW DRAWN RATHER THAN TYPED. The window used emoji and dingbats for search, pin, done, report, undo and the rest; those render at whatever size and weight the system feels like, and under Wine on Linux and macOS some of them didn't render at all. They're vectors now, in the colour of whichever theme you've picked.

NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THE TRACKER DOES HAS CHANGED - same tabs, same five views, same filters, same search, same undo, same counts, same ledger. Windows, Linux and macOS all got this in the same update rather than one waiting on the other.

THE LOOT VIEWS NOW KNOW WHERE EACH THING CAME FROM (contributed by Liminal Warmth). "What did I actually kill this for" and "what ended up in my bags" are different questions, and EQBuddy couldn't tell them apart - a corpse drop, a craft, a parcel and an auto-stored pickup all read the same. "(Disabled)" is now a real choice, on both desktops.

THE PLANE OF SKY TAB SHOWS YOUR QUESTS AGAIN, ONE PER REWARD (discussion #184, thanks bjstrange). Folding the widget's Sky card into the Quest Tracker last release re-grouped the tab by the TURN-IN NPC - and one NPC hands out every sky reward for a class, so all fourteen landed in a single undifferentiated list and "which pieces does this one still need" stopped being answerable. A MIS-CLICKED TICK CAN BE TAKEN BACK (same report - bjstrange lost three and had to work out from memory what had been checked). Ticking a checklist row saves immediately and said nothing, so a stray click was unrecoverable. A bar now names what just changed and offers ↶ undo, Ctrl+Z works too, and it steps back through as many as you need.

ITEMS EQBUDDY TICKED FOR YOU ARE MARKED (same report: "all are checked with no indication of anything needing manual adjustments"). When several classes want the same drop, the loot auto-tick has to pick one and can't know which of yours earned it - so it picks and flags the row. EQBuddy Mobile has been showing that * for months; both desktop builds were quietly drawing a bare tick. They now show it too, with a tooltip saying why, and moving the tick settles it.

THE CLASS FILTER STOPS EATING THE WINDOW when you tick more than a few classes. Selecting all sixteen turned the button into "BRD · BST · BER · CLR · DRU · ENC · MAG · MNK · NEC · PAL · RNG · ROG · SHD · SHM · WAR · WIZ", which pushed the mine/zone/held/done/all strip clean off the edge, and the chip row beside it was clipped mid-list. FIXED (discussion #186, thanks Kemble-Kemble) - THE QUEST TRACKER WAS CUT OFF ON A SECOND MONITOR AND COULDN'T BE SHRUNK. Its height was capped against your PRIMARY screen, so dragging it to a smaller one left it taller than that screen with no way back.
