FIXED (discussion #193, thanks wizen) - THE SKY AND EPIC CHECKLISTS TICKED ITEMS YOU NEVER LOOTED, sometimes for a dozen classes at once. When several classes want the same drop, EQBuddy is supposed to tick only the classes you actually play. With no class filter set, an empty class selection was being read as "every class matches" rather than "no class matches" - so ONE Wind Rune Azia ticked the Druid, Monk and Wizard tests together, and one Red Dragon Scales ticked both the Bard and Warrior epics. This became permanent in 1.88.0: the widget's old Sky and Epic cards used to keep a class selected, and when those cards folded into the Quest Tracker nothing set it any more. A shared drop with no class to attribute it to now ticks ONCE and wears a * for you to move, which is what it always did when a filter was set. If your checklists were already over-ticked, the fix stops it happening again but cannot know which ticks were wrong - set your classes in the Quest Tracker's class picker, then correct the rows; sorry for the tidying.

AND YOUR CLASS PICK NOW ACTUALLY DRIVES IT. Setting your class(es) in the Quest Tracker was always the intended way to scope these ticks, and it is now the ONLY thing that does - so it is worth setting even if you only play one character.

FIXED, FIFTH TIME (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, who has now sent six logs) - CHARM STILL DIDN'T ALWAYS REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. charm6.txt is a 3:28 charm on the Plane of Sky that announced its fade with no duration, and the cause is a new one again. He charmed Bzzazzt, put the pet on hold, and eight seconds later "Bzzazzt" landed a full five-hit round on him - so EQBuddy read that as his pet turning on him and threw the clock away fifteen seconds in. There were TWO Bzzazzt. The same-name guard added in 1.87.0 couldn't help, because the only proof it accepts is a creature attacking something with its own name, and these two never fought each other: the charmed one was busy with Eye of Veeshan (it killed it), the other was busy with him. But his pet had already said the thing that settles it - "Now holding, Master. I will not start attacks until ordered." A pet on hold does not start attacks, so a same-named attacker while yours is held is a different creature, and the claim now survives until the wear-off line settles it. Releasing the hold gives the ordinary rule back, and a nearby charmer's pet answering THEIR hold order is ignored. Verified by replaying his actual file: 'held 3:28', against no duration at all before.

FIXED (discussion #183, thanks TheLethean) - WAKING ONE MEZZED MOB COULD CLEAR THE CHIPS FOR ITS SAME-NAMED NEIGHBOURS. Waking a mob prints TWO lines - "Your Mesmerization spell has worn off of a skeleton." and "A skeleton has been awakened by Dorr." - and EQBuddy was dropping a chip for each, so every wake cost two. With a stack of identically-named mobs that reads exactly as "they all disappeared". The two lines are one break and are now paired: whichever arrives first drops the chip, the other is recognised as its partner. Order-proof, because his log prints the fade FIRST, which is why the existing guard never saw it. Two mobs genuinely broken at once still print two of each line, so both still count. His second log - which counts the losses per wake precisely - is what made this findable; a differently-named mob was never affected, and that detail is what proved it was name-scoped.

THE RESPAWN TIMER FINDS NAMED MOBS THE CATALOG HAS NEVER HEARD OF (discussion #185, thanks elderbit). Camping Focus Items he hit the gaps a hand-maintained list will always have — almost every named in The Hole, Chief Goonda in Western Karana - and pointed out that the log already tells us: EverQuest writes trash with an article ("an ogre shaman") and a named by its proper name ("Chief Goonda"). EQBuddy now reads that. Kill a proper-named mob that isn't in the catalog and it starts tracking it - with NO countdown, because one kill cannot know the cycle; the second kill measures it, and later shorter gaps tighten it. The row says "Found by EQBuddy" so you can tell it apart from the catalog and from your own entries, and you can type a duration over it or remove it.

IT IS DELIBERATELY CAUTIOUS, because an invented timer sends you to a camp that isn't up. Only YOUR OWN kills count - which is also what keeps pets and players out, the case elderbit flagged himself: they die as "X has been slain by Y", never as "You have slain X!". Gaps under 90 seconds and over six hours teach nothing. And his convention has one real exception we already knew about: Solusek's Eye's trash clockworks are called "CWG Model XA" with no article at all. Where the catalog lists a family's named (CWG Model EXG), that is a statement that its siblings are trash, and they are left alone - the same family rule that stopped them hijacking his clock in 1.88.3. The shipped catalog is still only ever edited by hand; discoveries live with your own learned timers.

QUEST REWARDS WRITTEN AS A TABLE COUNT AS REWARDS. The wiki reformatted the Soldier's Brooch page from a bullet list into a stat-comparison table, and this week's catalog refresh promoted the quest with an empty reward list - all eight class brooches gone. Our reader stopped at the table's first "=" sign. Fixed at the source and re-harvested.

THE WIDGET CAN FLOAT OVER FULLSCREEN EVERQUEST ON A MAC (thanks Liminal Warmth). Running EQBuddy under CrossOver, a fullscreen game painted straight over the widget - you played windowed or you didn't see EQBuddy. That's a Wine-on-macOS quirk rather than an EQBuddy bug: Wine hands a fullscreen game a window level no ordinary always-on-top window can beat. There's now an opt-in overlay mode that floats the widget over the game and stops a click on it pulling the game out of the foreground. It needs a one-time patch to Wine's Mac driver - see docs/CrossOver-macOS-overlay.md - and it is off by default and completely inert on Windows. The setup script builds that patch on your own machine from CodeWeavers' published source: we deliberately ship no prebuilt binary, because the step replaces a library inside your CrossOver install and you shouldn't have to trust an unreadable file from us to do it.

SPAWN TIMERS NO LONGER "LEARN" A RESPAWN FROM TWO DIFFERENT MOBS (thanks Liminal Warmth). In Solusek's Eye, killing an ordinary clockwork could start CWG Model EXG's 18-minute countdown - the typo-forgiving matcher bridged the whole CWG Model XA/XB/XC serial family onto the named - and then killing the REAL EXG at the bridge 93 seconds later taught EQBuddy that his respawn is 93 seconds, permanently. That gap was walk time between two different mobs, not a spawn cycle. The matcher now refuses name-family siblings (a shared name with a different last word is another mob, not a typo), and a countdown only learns from the named's own kills on both ends of a gap - placeholder kills still restart the clock, they just can't teach it a duration. The ▶ manual start also always takes effect now, even backdated behind a running timer. If a named of yours got stuck with an absurdly short timer, clear its duration in the Spawns window once to return to the catalog value.

FIXED (discussion #173, thanks KoboldCoterie again) - THE TITLE BAR COULD STAND YOUR CHARACTER'S NAME UP VERTICALLY, one letter per line, on Linux. Reserving room for the CPU/memory readout in 1.88.0 left the name too little space, and the name label wrapped instead of shortening - so a widget that had just stopped resizing itself started spelling K-o-b-o-l-d downwards in a title bar three times too tall. The name now stays on one line and ends in an ellipsis when it doesn't fit, which is what it should always have done. The keyboard fix he confirmed is unaffected.

CHARM PETS ARE CLAIMED MORE ACCURATELY - AND FEWER PETS THAT AREN'T YOURS (thanks chrstahl, discussion #177). When you charm something, the "it's yours now" line arrives about one cast time later, so EQBuddy now waits exactly that long PER SPELL: nine seconds for Cajole Undead, under four for Charm. One fixed wait could never fit both. Which spells are charms, and how long each takes, now comes straight from the wiki and refreshes weekly - so a new charm, or a corrected cast time, reaches you without anyone typing it in. That list is built from what each spell DOES rather than what it is called, which turned up a real culprit: Allure of Death - a necromancer mana regen - was being treated as a charm purely because of its name, so casting it could hand you a nearby enchanter's pet and credit its damage to you for as long as that pet lived. Four other innocently-named spells were doing the same. Bards also gain Solon's Bravura and Tunare's Request being recognised under both the spellings the game and the wiki use.

/PET WHO LEADER NOW SETTLES IT EITHER WAY (chrstahl's own suggestion). Ask your pet who its leader is and the answer is final: name you, and that pet is yours from that moment. Name somebody else - a nearby player's pet answering their question - and EQBuddy lets go of it. That is the only way to correct a pet it guessed wrong about while the guess is still costing you an accurate number, and it is worth putting on your charm macro or a hotkey if pet damage matters to you.

POTION BUFFS SHOW ON THE BUFF TRACKER (issue #167, thanks Liminal Warmth). THE QUEST TRACKER HAS ONE WAY IN NOW. Type what you actually know - the REWARD you want ("Wakizashi of the Frozen Skies"), an item in your bags, the quest's name, the NPC who gives it, or a zone - and the quest comes back, with 📌 to keep tracking it. That search already worked, but it sat under a "+ I have this" item-and-quantity row that won the eye completely; David missed the search entirely for weeks. The row is gone and the box now says what it takes.

AND A ⧉ SCAN BAGS BUTTON replaces what that row was for. Rather than typing in items you owned before EQBuddy could see them - spelling and all - copy /outputfile inventory, paste it in the game's chat, and EQBuddy reads your bags AND your bank exactly. FIXED - THE EQBUDDY MOBILE QR CODE COULD POINT AT AN ADDRESS YOUR PHONE CAN'T REACH. If your PC has Tailscale, Hyper-V, VirtualBox or WSL, those adapters have addresses that look exactly as private as your real Wi-Fi, and whichever one Windows happened to list first won the QR - so the scan just timed out, which looks like a firewall problem and isn't. EQBuddy now prefers the adapter that actually has a route to the internet, which is the one your tablet is on. If pairing has been failing for you, this is why.

SEARCHING THE QUEST TRACKER NO LONGER FREEZES IT. Typing rebuilt the whole list on every single keystroke, and with the full 1,172-quest catalog in view that meant nine rebuilds for a word like "Wakizashi" - the window appeared to hang. It now waits for you to stop typing, and shows the first 60 matches with a "+N more" line rather than laying out hundreds of cards you'd never scroll to.

ONE QUESTS CARD ON THE WIDGET, IN PLACE OF "Sky Quest" AND "Epics". Both of those cards carried a full tabbed checklist on the widget itself - fourteen class tabs, a search box, state filters - which is a lot of screen for something you read between pulls rather than during one. They are now a single "Quests" card that opens the Quest Tracker window, where all three tabs already live. The card still shows both scores at a glance ("Epic 1/12 · Sky 3/40"), your checklists still tick themselves as you loot with nothing open at all, and "Quest tracker…" has left the ⚙ menu because the card is the way in. If you had hidden both old cards, the new one starts hidden too; if you had either one showing, it shows. The Epic tab's "classic-doable only" filter moved into the Quest Tracker with it.

EQBUDDY MOBILE GETS THE WHOLE QUEST TRACKER. One "Quests" screen on your tablet or mobile device now carries the same three tabs as the PC window - Quests, Epic 1.0, Plane of Sky - with the same search box (rewards, items, quest names, NPCs, zones), the class chips and the full class picker on every tab, and the same cards: progress per turn-in item, ✔ ready, the wiki link. Tap 📌 to track a quest, tap Epic and Sky rows to tick them - every tap lands in the same place a desktop click does, so both screens always agree. Search runs ON the device: the PC sends the whole quest catalog once, so typing costs no round trips and answers as fast as the desktop does. The separate Epic-checklist and Sky-checklist screens folded into this one; a device that was showing them keeps its pick under the new name automatically.

FIXED, FOURTH TIME LUCKY (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, who has now sent five logs) - CHARM STILL DIDN'T ALWAYS REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. His latest log shows a 5-minute charm that announced its fade with no duration, and the cause is one nobody had considered: the creature had cast a damage-over-time spell (Choking) on him BEFORE he charmed it, and that spell kept ticking afterwards. EQBuddy read each tick as "my pet just turned on me", threw the clock away six seconds into the charm, and the real fade five minutes later had no landing left to measure. A tick is not a decision to attack - it is the tail of a spell cast before the charm existed - so ticks no longer break a charm. Genuine swings still do. This is why the previous three fixes missed it: all of them key on a real attack, and this charm ended with no attack at all. The mez tracker had already learned this exact lesson back in issue #32; charm never got the same guard.

FIXED ON LINUX AND macOS (discussion #169, thanks joma65) - YOUR WINDOWS CAME BACK AT THE TOP-LEFT CORNER every launch: the main widget, the spawns window and both chip stacks, all at 0,0 however carefully you had parked them. When a window closes, X11 and Wayland can report its position as 0,0 while it is being torn down - and EQBuddy wrote that number down as though you had dragged the window there. The two chip stacks already defended against this; the other windows did not, and the same trap catches a window OPENING too, because the desktop applies a move a moment after it is asked for. EQBuddy now records only a position it saw while the window was genuinely on screen, and if it never saw one it leaves your saved spot alone. Windows was never affected. If your positions were already flattened, they are yours to set once more - this stops them being lost again.

FIXED (discussion #169, thanks joma65) - LINUX AND macOS RAN A WHOLE SECOND COPY OF EQBUDDY EVERY TIME YOU LAUNCHED IT. Only the Windows build stopped a second copy starting; everywhere else every launch started another one, and because two widgets are undecorated, always on top, and restore to the same saved spot, they sat exactly on top of each other and looked like one. Each copy loads all your settings at startup and writes all of them back on any change, so whichever one saved last quietly reverted everything the other had changed - the likely reason the two "hide the widget" tick-boxes wouldn't stay ticked, while your window positions (identical in both copies) appeared to hold. Launching EQBuddy again now brings the running one to the front instead, on every platform, and a leftover lock file can never stop it starting. EQBuddy also records in error.log when something else changes settings.json underneath it, so this can never hide again.

FIXED (discussion #173, thanks KoboldCoterie) - ON LINUX, TURNING ON THE TITLE-BAR CPU/MEMORY READOUT COULD STOP THE KEYBOARD REACHING EVERQUEST. The readout's text got wider as the numbers grew, and because the widget sizes itself to its contents, every refresh resized a real always-on-top window - every three seconds, forever, whether or not anything else had changed. Over a fullscreen game on X11 that is enough to disturb it, and the reported symptom was exactly that: the mouse kept working and the keyboard stopped. The readout now reserves a fixed width and formats to a fixed shape, so a new sample repaints and nothing else. Nothing was wrong with the measurement itself and the numbers are unchanged. Windows was never affected, but it carried the same growing-text code and now shares the fixed one.

FIXED (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk) - CLASS DETECTION WORKS BOTH WAYS NOW. EQBuddy guesses your class from the log when you haven't picked one, and it knew only MELEE skills - so a caster who once produced a melee-ish line wore that class for the rest of the session, and nothing he did afterwards could argue back, because there was nothing in the table a caster could ever trigger. All sixteen classes can now produce evidence, drawn from the spell and AA catalogs EQBuddy already ships rather than a hand-typed list. Recent play outweighs what you were doing an hour ago, so swapping characters converges on the one you're actually playing. Where an item could have cast the spell it wants to see two different ones, so a borrowed clicky can't flip you the other way. And when the log is genuinely ambiguous it now says nothing instead of guessing - it was always labelled "(inferred)", and an honest blank is better than a confident wrong answer. This also fixes Shadow Knight and Paladin never being detected by Harm Touch or Lay on Hands, which print as spell damage and so missed the melee-only check entirely.

FIXED (discussion #175, thanks jlcrisp) - BEASTLORD WAS MISSING FROM EVERY CLASS PICKER. He spotted it on the buff-set picker, but one list feeds them all, so Beastlord was equally absent from the quest tracker, the Plane of Sky tab, the buff breakout and EQBuddy Mobile. The wiki is clear that Legends has sixteen classes; our list had fifteen, and it looks to have been read off the epic roster - Beastlord has no Epic 1.0, which is correct rather than an omission. It does have five Plane of Sky tests, and it now appears everywhere it should, abbreviated BST as the wiki writes it.

FIXED (discussion #176, thanks Fennec-Halas) - THE PALADIN GOLDEN HILT POINTED AT THE WRONG ISLE. EQBuddy sent you to Isle 2 and the Protector of Sky for Thelvorn, Blade of Light; it actually drops from the sphinxes, drakes and undine spirits on ISLE 7. Checked four ways against the wiki before changing it, including that Isle 2's boss drop list contains no Golden Hilt at all. Note the wiki's own Golden Hilt page still labels its quest link "Paladin Test of Compassion" when the quest is Paladin Test of Love - the link goes to the right page, only the label is wrong.

MOTES ARE WEIGHED, NOT JUST COUNTED (discussion #154, thanks EzraSmith). The Motes card now reports the upgrade experience your session's motes are actually worth, because a hundred Infinitesimal motes and a hundred Infinite ones are not the same hour. Checking the wiki's table to build it turned up two errors of our own that counting had hidden: we had Major and Greater the wrong way round, and we ranked the plain "Mote of Potential" at the bottom of the ladder when it is the fourth rung and worth 4. Void-Touched Potential is recognised too - it counts, and weighs nothing, because it raises a whole tier instead of adding experience.

FIXED (issue #153, thanks adndmike) - THE ALERT VOLUME SLIDER DID NOTHING TO YOUR OWN .WAV FILES, while it moved the seven built-in sounds perfectly. The slider was never the problem: your sound wasn't playing at all. If EQBuddy couldn't find the file you had picked - moved, renamed, on a drive that wasn't plugged in - it quietly played the Windows notification ding instead, and that one comes from Windows at Windows' volume, so 10% and 100% sounded identical. The built-ins ship with Windows and are always there, which is why they alone appeared to obey the slider. There is now no route left that the slider can't reach: a sound that has gone missing gets a banner naming the file, and Ding stands in at YOUR volume until you pick another. Same fix on Linux and macOS, where the fall-through was a console beep.

STILL OPEN in the same report: the two "hide the widget while the game isn't focused / isn't running" tick-boxes also came back off, and that has a different cause which we have not found yet. Nothing in the code turns them off, so we would rather say so than ship a guess. If this is happening to you, your ~/.config/EQBuddy/error.log is the thing that will crack it.

FIXED AGAIN (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange for a fourth log) - CHARM STILL LOST ITS HELD TIME when two creatures share a name. His log says it outright: "A greater ice bones slashes a greater ice bones." Your charmed one was fighting the uncharmed one, and the UNCHARMED one was hitting you - EQ's log identifies creatures only by name, so EQBuddy could not tell them apart and read it as your pet turning on you. The claim was dropped six seconds into a 32-second charm, so the fade had nothing left to measure. A pet that is demonstrably busy hitting something else no longer loses its claim to a same-named attacker; the wear-off line settles it instead. This is a different cause from the in-flight-swing fix in 1.85.0, which is why that one did not cover it.

FIXED (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk - who found this AND fixed it at the source) - SYMBOL OF PINZARN ALWAYS READ AS MISSING, however many times you cast it. EQBuddy watches for the exact text a buff prints when it lands, and the wiki had the wrong text on file for this one - so it was waiting for a line your log never contains. He corrected the wiki page; EQBuddy now has the real message and a 45-minute timer to go with it. Endure Magic, Poison, Disease, Cold and Fire also became trackable in 1.86.0, if you had been unable to add those.

FIXED (discussion #172, thanks bjstrange) - UNCHECKING A SKY QUEST ITEM LEFT THE QUEST LOOKING READY. Ticking the last item marks a quest ready to turn in; unticking it again updated the counters but not the list itself, so the ready label stayed put until something else forced a redraw. The list now refreshes exactly when a quest's readiness changes - and not on every tick, so checking off a long quest no longer loses your scroll position.

FORAGED ITEMS COUNT NOW (discussion #163, thanks wizen). The game announces a forage as "You have scrounged up ..." rather than a normal loot line, and EQBuddy was ignoring it entirely. Forages now appear on the Loot card and in the new recent-drops view with "Forage" as their source, which also means a foraged item can tick a quest or gear row like any other. A failed forage is still ignored - a miss is not a drop.

BUFF TIMERS NAME THE SPELL LINE INSTEAD OF QUOTING THE GAME (discussion #162, thanks DeusSilvam). A tracked buff used to be labelled with whatever the game printed - "You feel much faster" - while other lines already showed a proper name. 37 of the 163 tracked lines were like that; they now read "Haste line", "Cleric AC line", "Thorns damage shield", "Levitation" and so on. Nothing you have configured moves: these are display names only.

42 MORE BUFFS CAN BE TIMED (discussion #162, thanks DeusSilvam, who noticed his shaman spells were missing). Talisman of Altuna, Strength, Agility, Dexterity, Stamina and Spirit of the Puma are now tracked, along with 36 others - the Endure/Resist lines, Charisma, Health, Nimble, Feet like Cat and more. A WAY BACK IF AN UPDATE GOES WRONG (discussion #158, thanks n3cr0nk1tt3n for the idea and twidget76 for the report that prompted it). EQBuddy's updater lives inside the widget, so a build that won't start takes the route to its own fix with it - which is exactly what happened with 1.84.0. If an update ever leaves you with a widget that won't open, start that one instead and update from inside it. It appears only once there is a previous build to go back to, and uninstalling removes it.

THE LOOT CARD CAN SHOW EVERY DROP AS IT HAPPENED (discussion #160, thanks wizen). The sort row on the Loot card gains a third option, "recent": your session's raw loot in arrival order, newest first, instead of totals. It exists for long farms - when you have looted 200 HQ Lion Skins, a rare pelt appearing is a count going from 0 to 1, which looks exactly like the skin count going from 200 to 201. In arrival order it is simply the row that is not a Lion Skin. Runs of the same item collapse into one line with a count, so a streak cannot push the interesting drop off the end.

BUFF LOSSES CAN NAME A DEBUFF AS THE CAUSE (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk). The lost-buff history could already say "lost as X landed" when a nuke or a slow displaced one of your set buffs - but a PURE debuff deals no damage and is not a slow, so it landed in total silence and the buff it displaced was recorded as merely "faded". 615 detrimental spells now have their cast-on-you lines catalogued, so his documented case reads "lost as Malaise landed" instead. The window is deliberately tight and a shared line names every candidate rather than guessing one - a wrong cause in a bug report to the game devs is worse than no cause.

FIXED, AND THE REASON TO UPDATE (discussion #158, thanks twidget76) - EQBUDDY 1.84.0 WOULD NOT START if you had the Epic card's "classic-doable only" filter ticked. It appeared in Task Manager using no CPU, never reached the taskbar, and never opened a window - and because the failed launch left a process behind, a second double-click did nothing either. Restoring that checkbox at startup called into a part of the app that had not been built yet, which was a mistake introduced by 1.84.0's internal reorganisation of the quest checklists. If this hit you, nothing was damaged: your settings, history and logs were untouched the whole time. An automated launch test now runs with that filter ON, because the reason this reached anyone is that the old test only covered it OFF.

FIXED (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, whose log finally cracked it) - CHARM SOMETIMES DIDN'T REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. If the creature was mid-swing at the instant your charm landed, the game resolved that attack round anyway - and EQBuddy read your brand-new pet hitting you as the charm breaking, throwing away the clock one second after starting it. Minutes later the real fade had nothing left to measure, so the "held M:SS" went missing while the fade message itself printed as normal. That is why it looked random and moved between mobs: it depended entirely on the creature's swing timer. A hit within 3 seconds of the landing is now the tail of that round rather than a break.

THE GEAR LOCKER NOW TELLS YOU WHAT TO SWAP IN (discussion #145, thanks skwayb). It already flagged which of your items were ⬇ outclassed by others you own; what it never said was which one is actually on your character. Now it does - ★ marks what you're wearing in each slot, and anything in your bags that beats it on every stat both items carry is marked ⬆ upgrade over worn X. Two deliberate refusals: an item class-locked away from you is never suggested, and a plain item never claims to beat a worn "+N", because the wiki lists base stats and an upgraded item reads lower here than it really is - being told to unequip your best piece would be worse than being told nothing. As always this reads your bags against your own character and nobody else's.

YOUR LOGS ARE KEPT NOW, NOT EMPTIED (discussion #146, thanks wizen). EQBuddy tidies up finished session logs so they don't grow without bound - but until now the out-of-the-box behaviour was to empty the file and keep nothing, which is a decision nobody asked it to make. Archiving is ON by default from this release, and it is switched on for existing installs too: each finished session is saved to Logs\archive as eqlog_name_server_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.txt, and Reset session splits the log there rather than letting it run on. They're text files, as wizen pointed out - the space is worth less than the history. If you would rather have it back, one untick in ⚙ Options → "Keep a timestamped copy before emptying" returns the old behaviour, and it stays off once you set it. EQBuddy never deletes anything in Logs\archive.

FIXED (discussion #152, thanks Snagglefern) - MEZ AND SPAWN CHIPS CREPT UP THE SCREEN, one chip's height every time the stack emptied and came back, if you use "grow upwards". A grow-up stack has to remember its BOTTOM edge, since its top moves with the chip count - but that was being measured as the window closed, when its height already reads as zero, so what got saved was really the TOP edge. Next time it opened it subtracted a chip from that and landed one row higher. Fixed at the source, and the spawn stack had the identical bug waiting.

FIXED (discussion #144, thanks n3cr0nk1tt3n) - THE BOTTOM CARD COULD BE CUT OFF with no way to scroll to the rest of it, and whether it happened depended on your widget size slider - the Epics card showed it first, being the longest. The card list lives under the size transform, so the limit it gets is measured in different units than the screen figure it was being handed; the two only agreed at 100%. Away from that, the list's idea of its own room drifted from what the window could show, and once it thought it had more room than existed the last card was simply clipped. Now converted properly, and re-derived whenever you move the slider. Spotting that it changed WITH the scaling is what made this findable.

NEW - EQBUDDY NOW RENDERS UNDER WINE (PR #148, contributed by liminalwarmth - this one is entirely their work): players running the Windows build through Wine on Linux or CrossOver on macOS got empty boxes instead of every icon. Wine prefixes ship no Segoe fonts, and Wine's text engine only ever looks at the app's PRIMARY font - so EQBuddy now bundles one font containing everything it draws, text and icons alike, and switches to it only when it detects Wine. On real Windows nothing changes at all. They also added a test that fails the build if anyone adds an icon the bundled font doesn't cover, so it can't quietly rot.

NEW - EQBUDDY MOBILE (BETA) IS OUT OF PREVIEW: put EQBuddy on the phone or tablet already sitting beside your keyboard. Click the 📱 button in the title bar, scan the code with the device's camera, and its browser becomes a second screen - a live zone map, spawn timers, mez chips, buffs, combat breakdowns, session stats, loot, XP, and your Epic/Sky/Gear checklists. Each device picks WHICH of those it shows and in what order, so the tablet propped up beside you and the phone in your pocket can show completely different things. Nothing to install on the device, and it updates with EQBuddy itself.

It is OFF until you turn it on, and it stays on your own Wi-Fi. No account, no cloud, no telemetry: the pages are served by EQBuddy.exe straight to your device, and nothing leaves your network. You decide what may be sent at all (Options → Behavior → EQBuddy Mobile), and "New code" instantly locks out every device you have paired.

Worth knowing up front: Windows will ask to allow EQBuddy through the firewall the first time you switch it on - if you dismiss that prompt, devices simply can't connect and nothing will say why, so switch it off and on again to get the prompt back. Guest/public Wi-Fi that isolates devices from each other will also block it. And browsers won't hold a screen awake over plain HTTP, so bump your device's screen timeout if you're camping.

🧭 Travel route (right-click → Travel route…): pick any zone and get hop-by-hop directions from where you're standing, from client-mined atlas data plus the wiki's boat and port connections — the same distance graph that already sorts your quests by "close to me".
🔎 Quest search went catalog-wide: search all 900+ wiki quests by name, reward, needed item, or NPC — not just the ones your zone offers. Found a weird drop? Type it in and see who wants it.

🍎 EQBuddy runs on macOS now — thank quasarj (PR #90) for building the Mac side of the Avalonia app. Faction lines read right at both ends of the scale too: a faction at rock bottom now says so instead of claiming "maxed" (elderbit's sharp catch, #86). Plus the storage engine moved to SQLitePCLRaw 3, and the whole widget got another idle-cost pass on top of 1.52's.

This release was shaped in the field: thanks to Bigmatt500, Kerdude, KentCarmine, and dandrews2930 for the asks, testing, and patches that steered the week — and to everyone dropping reports in Discussions. Keep them coming; most of what's on this page started there.

A week of features earned a day of tuning: EQBuddy now does close to NOTHING while nothing happens. Expanded cards used to rebuild themselves every second even when idle — they now repaint only when the log actually produced an event (a 10-second heartbeat keeps per-hour rates honest during AFKs). Item tooltips stopped re-reading their wiki cache from disk every second. Quest-ledger saves batch instead of writing the whole file at every loot. And with "hide while the game is unfocused" on, a hidden widget now truly rests. Net effect: less CPU, less garbage-collection, fewer chances for a Defender scan to hitch your loot moment — same widget, lighter footprint.

The README grew up with the app: fresh screenshots of the Sky checklist, Drops by Creature with its ✦ wiki flags, the Quest Tracker mid-"ready", the session picker, and the cursor ring — plus documentation for everything the last week added. If you've been describing EQBuddy to a guildmate from memory, the page finally does it justice.

Linux: FIXED a crash-on-every-launch loop (issue #82, caught on Bazzite): closing EQBuddy while minimized to the dashboard saved a state the next launch couldn't survive — the breakout tiles tried to appear before the main window existed, and the failure killed the app before it drew anything. Breakouts now wait their turn, and no breakout problem can take the widget down again. (If you're currently stuck: update, or set "Minimized": false in ~/.config/EQBuddy/settings.json.)

.* Watch rules speak regex now (KentCarmine's ask, #83): a new toggle beside the Match box treats it as a .NET regular expression — "CH (-->|on) Tank" catches both spellings of the raid call in one rule. Case-insensitive like everything else; an invalid pattern matches nothing and explains itself in the Match box's tooltip; runaway patterns are cut off at 100 ms so the log pipeline never stalls. Regex mode travels in rule share strings.

⭕ Cursor ring (Bigmatt500's ask, #81 — "I often lose my tiny cursor"): right-click → Cursor ring drapes an accent-colored halo around your pointer, click-through and focus-proof like the grid overlay. Dark under-stroke so it reads on snow and shadow alike; survives restarts until you toggle it off.

Sold items grew up (Snagglefern's follow-up, #74): the Money card's auto-sold list is now clickable for item info and carries the same quest badges and wiki tooltips as the Loot card — "if an item is unknown on the wiki I definitely sold it" was a fair cop. Sold drops were already feeding Drops by Creature and the ✦ pack; now the Money card admits they're items, not just coins.

This week's wiki catch-up landed via the first scheduled knowledge refresh (PR #84): 2 new quests, the Kobold Molars pages' community edits folded in, and the quest catalog stays current without anyone remembering to run anything.

FIXED: stacked corpse loot counted as zero (#80, Snagglefern's bone-chip census — 100 chips, 25 counted). "--You have looted 2 Bone Chips--" never matched the loot parser, which only knew "a/an"; every multi-pickup vanished entirely rather than counting as one. Stacks now count in the Loot card, Drops by Creature, drop rates, and the ✦ wiki pack. If your favorite farm suddenly looks twice as generous — it always was.

Archive review grew a SESSION PICKER (Snagglefern's follow-up, #74): reviewing a log that holds several sessions — the pre-splitter giants — now asks which one, newest first, with dates and durations. The chosen session replays alone: its drops, its zone, its wiki pack, nothing bleeding in from the sessions around it. Files made by the log splitter are one session each and skip the question entirely. A 10 MB archive is finally days of reviewable evenings instead of whichever session happened to be last.

⏪ Review any archived log (Snagglefern's ask, #74 — they kept every log precisely to mine drops for the wiki): right-click → "Review an archived log…", pick a file, and EQBuddy replays it read-only. The title bar turns amber while you're in the past; one click on it returns to the live log. Drops by Creature and ✦ Copy for wiki work against the reviewed session, nothing double-writes to Session History, and your live character is re-followed the moment you're back. (A multi-session file shows its LAST session — archives made by the splitter are one session each, which is the point of the splitter.)

Linux: click-through works again — it lost its only trigger when the global hotkeys were removed (issue #7). Now it's in the right-click menu, with the same amber 🔒 unlock chip as Windows parked beside the widget: a window that ignores clicks can't be clicked back to life, so the chip is the one solid thing left. Engages only when X11 actually grants it — Wayland gets an honest log line instead of a lying checkbox. The version line in the Linux menu also opens the GitHub page now.

↕ Drag the widget's BOTTOM EDGE to make it taller or shorter — text size stays put (that's still the corner grip's job). A Reddit ask from a player who scaled up for readability and got a scrollbar for their trouble: now you choose how much room the widget takes. Double-click the edge to go back to fit-the-screen, and your choice survives restarts and scale changes.

The Sky Quest card scrolls (dandrews2930's third same-day PR, #78 — fixing hstahl76's report #77 within the hour): each class tab caps its height and scrolls, so 16 quests no longer shove the card past your screen.

Kobold Molars count now (#79 — Frankthetankk's diagnosis was right): the quest parser only understood "give/hand/turn in" grammar, but repeatable turn-in loops say "each [[Kobold Molar]] that is TURNED IN" or "a chance to DROP a" — both Molars quests now track their molar and flag ready when you hold one. The wider grammar enriched 123 quests' turn-in lists, every addition still vouched for by the wiki's own Quest Items category.

Your /consider lines now feed the wiki pack (#65): each con names a level — the only place the log ever does — so the observed stat block and page skeleton carry a per-creature level range. Con a spawn once to seed it; con the ones that feel different to widen the honest range.
Click the version line in the right-click menu to open EQBuddy's page (TropicMike's ask, #76) — the share-with-a-guildmate link is finally one click away.

🔊 Alerts can SPEAK now, contributed by dandrews2930 (PR #71): each watch rule gets an S toggle that reads the alert aloud with the Windows voice — "Spirit of the Puma faded off you" — with duplicate lines suppressed so a chain of fades doesn't chant at you. Speech travels in rule share strings too. (Windows only for now; the toggle is honest about it on Linux.)

Also from PR #71: a Buff filter for Spell Fade rules — one rule that hears ANY cataloged beneficial buff fade (stat buffs, protections, haste, clarity, movement…) — and a searchable buff picker for By-name rules: start typing and pick from the 903-spell fade catalog instead of spelling Ervaj from memory.

Sky Quest rewards get their own checkbox (chrstahl's ask, #73, filed hours after 1.46 shipped): the reward line now marks "I turned this in" — completing it checks off its items and dims them, unchecking reopens the quest. Manual on purpose: the log shows nothing reliable at the NPC hand-over, so the player is the source of truth, including for quests done before the card existed.

The wiki catch-up is now automatic: a weekly knowledge refresh re-harvests eqlwiki-derived catalogs (incremental — only pages that actually changed) and opens a review PR with the delta. Its first pass already landed here: 2 new quests, 8 updated Plane of Sky Tests pages, and the Wind Runes joining the don't-vendor list — the community updated the wiki to match the Sky checklist the same day it shipped. Curated data (spawn timers, AAs, mez/CC lists) is never auto-written; a human reviews the flags.

☁ Sky Quest checklist, contributed by dandrews2930 (PR #70): a new overlay card tracks all 222 Plane of Sky quest turn-in items — a tab per class, reward-grouped checkboxes, each item's isle and source under its name. Loot ticks boxes by itself: win a quest item and it checks off, scoped to the class tab you actually use (five classes each need a Wind Rune Azia; yours is the one that gets it). Progress persists across sessions, restarts, and log splits.

The ↻ button finishes joeymavity's log-splitting ask (#52): with "Keep a timestamped copy" on, Reset session stats now splits the live log on the spot — everything so far moves to Logs\archive under the exact eqlog_name_server_STAMP.txt naming and a fresh log begins immediately, mid-play, no waiting for the session to go stale. 1.38 shipped the janitor half of the original request; this was the half still owed. (Tools that tail the log with their own byte offset — GINA and kin — will want a restart after a split, same as after any cleanup.)
Linux: the Avalonia janitor now honors the archive checkbox — it was truncating stale logs without keeping the copy the option promised.

Watch rules travel now: the ⤴ on any rule row copies it as a compact EQB1 share string sized for guild chat or Discord, and the import box under the rule list turns one back into a rule — with a preview of exactly what it does BEFORE you accept it. Imports are rebuilt field by field (fresh identity, custom sound paths never leave the sharer's machine), so a share string can never do anything the rule editor couldn't. Your raid's CH-chain cues are one paste away from the whole channel.

▦ Grid overlay (garr's guild-mate energy, discussion #34): right-click → Grid overlay drapes a faint click-through grid over your whole desk for lining up game UI elements — stronger lines every fourth square, spacing slider in Options (live while it's up), and it never eats a click or steals focus. Toggle off in the same menu when everything's finally straight.

Divine Invocation's proc heals now carry its name in the HPS tracker: the invocation heals your party's lowest-health member for the mana of whatever you cast, and that heal line names no spell — it used to pile up under "Unknown". While the divine invocation is being recited, unattributed heals are attributed where they belong.

The wiki contribution pack gained an OBSERVED STAT BLOCK per creature (Frankthetankk's field list, round two): zone at kill time (not wherever you're standing at export), money per kill in the wiki's own low–high range format — one sample honestly labeled as one sample — and faction hits with counts against your kill count, including "no hits observed across N kills", because a confirmed absence saves the next tester the experiment. Everything framed for reconciliation: compare, don't overwrite.

The multiSpawn doctrine went global: every zone's multi-location names (EC griffons, Lesser Fay brownie guards, Permafrost elite guards, Skyfire shadow drakes, the West Karana ogre shrine, Crushbone's warden) now carry the flag, so sibling kills and sightings can't poison their clocks anywhere. And spawn cycles with several placeholders finally work: Queen Dracnia's webmaster/lurker/purifier rotation restarts her clock from any of the three.

Spawn timers grew a doctrine, forged in a live Crushbone session: for ACTUAL nameds, an observation beats a lock — a named acting in the final stretch of its countdown out-measures even a "trusted" catalog clock (only your own typed values rank higher). For mobs that spawn in several places (Royal Guard, the trainers, the taskmasters — now flagged multiSpawn), the opposite: sightings and re-kill gaps prove nothing when siblings roam, so their clocks are kill-driven only, and any noise they'd already learned heals itself on your next kill. Also fixed: "orc trainee" no longer restarts the Orc Trainer clock — fuzzy name matching now knows wiki typos live at the front of names while sibling ranks inflect the end. The Crushbone trio runs its measured 8:00 (Adaptive tier), verified at the camps.

Mez durations, third time honest (rahvynn's report): 1.43's sanity ceiling clipped genuine mote-upgraded durations — a 44s Mesmerization shrank to its 24s base. The truth is simpler than any cap: a Legends mez holds a FIXED duration unless damage breaks it, and broken mezzes never reach the learner — so the tracker now trusts the latest clean fade in BOTH directions. Chain-mez artifacts and stale values alike heal on the very next honest observation, and long upgraded durations stick.

FIXED: the default "CC broke" rule pinged when a mob stunned YOU (rahvynn again — "You are no longer stunned." joined the fade catalog in 1.42 and the CC filters heard it). Self-recovery lines no longer satisfy CC filters, which mean "MY control of a mob ended"; By-name and Any-spell rules still hear your own buffs fade, as designed.

✦ wiki flagging, first field report applied (Frankthetankk): apostrophes now fold when comparing against wiki loot lists ({{:Packmasters Lash}} vs "Packmaster's Lash" was a false ✦), the contribution pack adds a paste line + edit link for each ITEM page's own Drops-from list, and drops carry their last-seen log time so you can find the moment in your own log again.

Spawn timers learn from SIGHTINGS: a named acting in your log before its chip says DUE proves the respawn already happened — the countdown completes on the spot (chip flips DUE, alert fires) and the observed cycle becomes the learned timer. Re-kill learning could never catch a slightly-long timer, because kill-to-kill gaps include the time you take to notice and kill the spawn. Twin protection: only the final fifth of a countdown accepts sightings, so same-named camps (looking at you, Crushbone taskmasters) can't finish each other's clocks. Your own typed timer values are never overwritten — but the chip still flips DUE when the mob is provably up.

FIXED: mez chips showing impossible durations (Taendar's report — Mesmerization V wearing a 1:10 timer on a 24-second mez). Chain-mez artifacts from an old version could write inflated durations into the learned file, and "only ever learn longer" meant they never healed. Learned durations now have a sanity ceiling (double the spell's base — real rank upgrades like 24s→36s still learn fine), and your install quarantines any old poison automatically on update.

Dismissing a breakout window with its ✕ now announces itself on the alert banner with the re-enable path (⚙ Options → Breakout windows) — the ✕ is a small target floating over a game screen, and a stray click could silently hide a window forever (ask David where his DPS breakout went).
FIXED: dismissing the last spawn-timer chip left a ghost chip painted until the stack closed — a bug Don Thompson caught while porting the chips to Linux, fixed on both sides.

Linux/Avalonia: Don Thompson's parity work through 1.32 is merged — breakout windows (damage/healing/pet), the full encounter review in Session History, mez chips, target drops on the Loot card, item info popups, Send feedback, alert volume with proper per-backend handling, and per-rule banner colors. The Linux build is catching up fast.

Drops by Creature now knows what EQLWIKI doesn't: an amber ✦ marks every drop that's missing from the creature's wiki page — including pages with empty loot lists and creatures with no page at all (headers say which). A new ✦ Copy for wiki button builds a paste-ready contribution pack: each creature gets its direct edit link and a block in the wiki's own house style, with rarity labels suggested only when your kill count can honestly carry them (10+ kills, using the wiki's published bands). Nothing publishes automatically — you review and save on the wiki (Frankthetankk's ask, #65; auto-publish waits on the wiki admins' blessing).

Watch rules now hear YOUR OWN buffs fade: the wear-off catalog grew from 61 hand-fed lines to 386 straight from the wiki — 903 spells covered. When a buff fades off YOU the log prints flavor text ("The spirit of the puma departs."), never the spell's name; now a By-name Spell Fade rule on Spirit of the Puma just works, soloing included (skulldugger's ask, #64).

Linux: the update banner now sends you straight to EQBuddy-linux-x64.tar.gz instead of a release page whose biggest button is a Windows installer (promised when #56 closed). Falls back to the release page if CI hasn't attached the tarball yet.

Quest loot marking, round two (an evening of live Crushbone testing): loot lines stay NORMAL text — a small 🗺 next to the name is the quest marker now, and it's on EVERY loot surface: the Loot card, target drops, the minimized 🎒 Loot breakout, and Drops by Creature. Click the 🗺 → its quests in the Quest Tracker; if only the wiki's Quest Items category vouches for it, the item's own wiki page opens instead. Item names still click through to item info.

Quest coverage jumped: pages that list requirements as bullet points (The Falchion style) now parse — 531 quests with turn-in items (was 458), 2,109 items known (was 1,188). And the badge covers the wiki's whole Quest Items category, so pieces like Blue Orc Head and Sealed Note mark properly. Watch for the 🗺 BEFORE your loot window auto-sells something a quest wants.

Creature pages that exist but list no drops now say so — "the wiki page lists no drops yet" beats "nothing known", and points at Drops by Creature… as the way to teach the wiki. Pages that fill common_loot instead of known_loot parse too.
Berserker rune tracking (ahaselden, PR #54) and Don Thompson's Avalonia parity work continue in the background — Linux players, your build is catching up fast.

Quest Tracker counts got honest: items the log sees LEAVE now subtract — merchant sales, destroys, and merges (two belts becoming one is minus one; looting a belt straight into a merge is zero, not plus one). "Ready ×17" when you own one super-belt is history. Counters rebuilt once from your log under the new rules; your manual counts, pins, hides, and completions were untouched.

The minimized 📈 XP chip now shows XP/HOUR (with the level ETA) instead of total percent — minimized is farming mode, and the rate is the number you actually watch (MorrolanTV's ask, filed an hour before this shipped).
Items acquired before EQBuddy could see your log still need one "+ I have this" — the log can't reach into the past. Everything after that stays true on its own.

Quest Tracker: the class filter is now MULTI-SELECT — Legends characters can run up to three classes, so pick yours from the checkbox list (the button shows "PAL · NEC" style) and quests any of them can do stay visible. Remembered per character, so your alts each keep their own set.

FIXED: upgraded loot now counts for quests — "Crushbone Shoulderpads +2" folds to the base item everywhere quests look, so tiered drops show green in the Loot list, the 🗺 jumps to the right quests, and the tracker counts them (caught live, mid-fight, same-day).

FIXED: common creatures with zone-split wiki pages ("Orc Legionnaire (Crushbone)" vs "(Deathfist)") resolve again — a broken wiki redirect could dead-end the Target-drops lookup at "nothing known." The lookup now reads through zone suffixes and prefers the page matching the zone you're standing in (also caught live, mid-fight).

ZOOM ANYTHING: Ctrl + mouse wheel over any EQBuddy window scales it — breakouts, Quest Tracker, Drops, Spawns, History, Options, item popups — up to 250%, remembered per window (garr71's 4K report). The same gesture on the main widget drives the widget-size setting, and on spawn/mez chips drives the chips slider. One habit for the whole app.

READABLE EVERYWHERE: every text button (Copy CSV, + Add watch rule, Next ▶ …) got real high-contrast styling — fill, border, and ink that adapt to your theme. On light themes like Solarized they were nearly invisible ghosts; not anymore.

NEW: Drops by creature… (right-click menu) — every creature you've looted this session with observed drop rates (kill counts always shown), filterable, and exportable as text or CSV. Built for LeBigNasty's plan to feed corrected drop tables back to eqlwiki for revamped zones — if you camp PoSky/Hate/Fear, your observations can make everyone's Target-drops smarter.

Quest Tracker: an ERA dropdown hides quests from beyond the world's current era (≤ Kunark hides Velious; unmarked quests always show) — twidget76's idea. Berserker joined the class filter (also twidget76 — Legends' fifteenth class was missing).

Log cleanup can now ARCHIVE first: Options → "Keep a timestamped copy before emptying" saves each finished session as eqlog_name_server_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.txt in Logs\archive — joeymavity's ask, for people who want raw history kept.

Also merged today from contributors: Don Thompson's two Avalonia/Linux parity PRs (spawn windows, What's-new, options fixes) and ahaselden's rune absorption tracking (rune gains count as self-healing; blocked-hit streaks show in the Healing card).

Two big EXPANDED BETA features below — built in one day from your reports, and shaped by what you send next. Tell us what's confusing, wrong, or missing via the ✉ Send feedback button; that loop built everything you see here.

NEW (beta): 🗺 QUEST TRACKER — right-click menu or the 🗺 in the Loot header. 914 wiki quests matched against what you loot (plus a "+ I have this" box for pre-EQBuddy inventory). Three views: MINE (your items and 📌-pinned quests), ZONE (everything workable where you're standing — including dialogue chains with no items), ALL (browse). Each card: rewards up top (hover for wiki stats, click to open the page), turn-in progress with the same hover, giver/level/class, how many zones away the turn-in is (hover for the route — zone connections courtesy of eqltools.com), a 📌 to track, ✕ to dismiss. Filter by class. Click ✔ ready when you hand in — it consumes the items from your counts and marks it done (repeatables show "ready ×3" style counts instead of disappearing).

NEW (beta): quest loot shows GREEN in the Loot lists with a small 🗺 — green means a real quest wants that item, so think before you vendor it. Click the 🗺 to see exactly which quests, and pin the ones you care about. Dismissing a quest (✕) un-greens items only it wanted.

NEW: 🔮 MOTES gets its own card — every Mote of … Potential tier with counts and motes/hour, sorted by the ladder, counting both looted and stored-as-currency motes (flipwon's idea, filed through Send feedback). Star it for the mini pill.
Honest limits worth knowing: the game never logs hand-ins (that's what the ✔ click is for), the ledger starts counting from this update forward, and "zones away" counts a boat ride as one hop.

New Options slider: Chips & alerts size — scales the spawn timer chips, mez chips, and the alert banner together, up to 200%, separately from the widget (jlewisnj's 4K report through Send feedback). Drag it with Options open and watch the ★ alert tile resize live.
Breakout windows now resize from ANY side or corner, like a normal window — grab an edge and go (the corner grip stays as the visible hint; double-click it to auto-size again).

"Open wiki page" in the Item info popup works again — the window's drag handler was quietly stealing the click (thanks twidget76, filed through Send feedback). Same fix applied to clickable item names everywhere.

Named mobs with "The" names show their drops — The Prophet in Crushbone was coming up empty because the wiki page keeps its "The" and EQBuddy's lookup didn't. And when no exact name matches at all, a fuzzy wiki search now backstops the lookup (typos and punctuation drift resolve; a wrong creature never sneaks in).

FIXED: EQBuddy was silently swallowing Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen browser tab) and a few other shortcuts from EVERY app on your PC — the global hotkeys registered system-wide. They're gone entirely (thanks to the sharp-eyed Reddit report). Everything they did is on the widget itself: – for mini mode, right-click for camp markers and click-through.
Click-through moved to the right-click menu, with a small 🔒 chip beside the widget while it's on — click the chip to interact again (a click-through window can't be clicked to unlock itself).

✕ on a breakout window now hides it for good — its ⭐ chip stays on the mini pill, and Options → Breakout windows has checkboxes to bring any window back (thanks Frankthetankk, reported through Send feedback within an hour of 1.33.0).
The beta features grew up fast — one afternoon of live testing and your feedback produced everything below. Keep it coming via the new GREEN ✉ button, now right in the title bar.

NEW (beta): Loot breakout — star 🎒 and minimize: while you fight, the window shows what the creature can drop (your counts and % first, wiki drops behind, duplicates like "+2" tiers folded together). /consider something and it targets that instead — and multi-creature pulls show the whole group's possible loot merged, since the log can't know which one you've targeted. Hover any item for its wiki info (fetched on the spot); click to open its eqlwiki page. A Target | Session toggle flips to what you've looted.
NEW (beta): Watch breakout — pin 📌 any watch rule and minimize: a floating window shows every pinned rule with counts and per-hour rates (CrispyPigeon131's mote-window idea).

Breakout windows now RESIZE: drag the ⋰ grip and the list scrolls inside whatever size you set (double-click the grip to auto-size again). The damage/healing/pet windows also gained sort links — total · hits · avg · dps.

Regen songs finally show as healing: Hymn of Restoration ticks carry no amounts in the log, so EQBuddy now ESTIMATES — and since instruments and ranks raise the real number, you can type your true hp/tick into Options and your number wins (read it off the heal text over your head).
Sort the Loot list by name or count (Klona11), and a new Options toggle hides the widget while the game is running but not focused — alt-tab friendly (sicliffe-cloud).
A second EQBuddy launch can no longer crash on startup — fix contributed by ahaselden. Also patched a security advisory in the bundled SQLite library.

This release's new features are BETA — they work, but they're young. Try them and tell us what's confusing, broken, or missing via the new Send feedback… tool below. Your reports shape what they become.

NEW (beta): Breakout windows — star ⚔ dps, ✚ hps, or the new 🐾 pet star (top of the Combat card) and minimize: small floating bar charts show your damage, your healing, and your pet's damage by ability, each switchable between the current fight and the whole session. Drag them anywhere; ✕ hides one until you next minimize.

NEW (beta): Target drops — while you fight, the Loot card lists what the creature can drop (eqlwiki) with your own counts this session and honest drop percentages. Hover an item for its stats, click for full info. Toggle in Options.

NEW: Send feedback… in the right-click menu — writes up a feature request or bug report and opens it on GitHub Discussions for you to review and post. Nothing is ever sent by the app itself; you post it, under your account, after reading every word.

Every crowd-control spell in the game now counts for "Any crowd control" watch rules — the game has 87 stun spells and EQBuddy knew 6, so enchanter stuns like Color Flux never fired alerts (thanks chaosrah). Also from chaosrah: pick a color per alert rule (the ● dot in Options) so a mez break and a heal fade look different at a glance.

Alerts stopped talking over each other: several alerts in the same moment now play ONE sound, complete, instead of clips cutting each other off — and an alert for one creature no longer silences the same alert for a different creature seconds later.
NEW (beta): AA tracking — the Progress card lists every ability you own with what it does (from eqlwiki, all 144 abilities). Remembered per character, even after log cleanup.

NEW: Item info — click any item in the Loot section (or search in the popup) to see its stats, vendor value, who drops it, who sells it, and what quests want it, straight from eqlwiki. Cached for a week; works offline from cache.

Loot the game auto-stores now counts: motes routed to currency and pelts sent to the tradeskill depot write a special log line EQBuddy didn't know — mote watch rules were missing every stored mote (thanks joeymavity + shururuun for the exact lines).
Alerts were playing at HALF volume this whole time — a player-found bug (thanks gl_tchd). Now full volume, with an Alert volume slider in Options.
Right-click any spawn chip to dismiss it, even mid-countdown (thanks anyhow188).
The Watch rules guide was rewritten with clearer wording contributed by chaosrah, and the spell-class dropdown finally explains itself. A Nisch Mas Mender joins the Splitpaw catalog (chaosrah again).

AA potions count correctly: the potion's doubled gains use a different log line EQBuddy didn't know, and gains were counted as events rather than points — potioned sessions logged zero or half. Both fixed (thanks twill713 for the exact line).

Spawn timers understand renamed mobs: Legends gives classic named new proper names ('the ghoul lord' is Hoptor Thaggelum) — the catalog now carries aliases, starting with Hoptor (thanks chrstahl, again).

Measured spawn clocks now outrank kill-learning: mobs that spawn in several places at once (Orc Taskmaster, Royal Guard…) tricked the self-tightening timers with fast re-kills. Where a zone's clock has been measured (Crushbone's 12:18), learning stands down and old bad learned values clean themselves up. Your typed edits still beat everything.

Mez timers stopped lying in both directions: a broken mez can no longer teach its break-length as the spell's 'duration' (the 7-second Mesmerize incident), and learned durations now snap to the game's 6-second server tick so timers don't run past the real wake-up (verified against 1,000+ logged tick intervals).
On a portrait monitor, the widget can finally use the full screen height — it was sizing against your primary monitor even when living on a different one.

Upper Guk spawn timers actually fixed: Legends renamed the zone to "The City of Guk" — a name no classic source predicted — so EQBuddy didn't recognize it and started no timers there. Confirmed from chrstahl's log lines (thanks for testing and reporting from the field!); those exact lines are now the automated test.

Guk spawn timers fixed: Legends renamed Lower Guk ('The Ruins of ANCIENT Guk' — classic said 'Old'), and the unrecognized zone name silently disabled every timer there. EQBuddy now knows the Legends zone names, and zones can carry aliases so future renames are one-line fixes.

Guk catalog audit: the froglok shin knight added to Lower Guk (it roams both Guks), and the froglok warden + ancient croc got their 16:30 timers. If a timer runs long, your kills still tighten it automatically.

Mez chips, round two (thanks again Vellum670): a mezzed mob's chip no longer disappears when its same-named twin wakes up and fights — the woken one's combat is recognized as its own, kills are attributed to it, and re-mezzing it adds a fresh chip without touching the sleeper's.
Mez chips, day-one fixes (thanks Vellum670 for same-day field testing): re-mezzing now REFRESHES the countdown — chain-mezzing works as you'd expect, and bard pulse songs keep their chip alive.
Same-named mobs caught by an AoE mez get separate, numbered chips ('orc pawn (2)'), and a break clears one of them, not all.

Chips no longer vanish mid-mez: damage-over-time ticks from a spell cast before the mez don't count as 'the mob woke up', and a chip whose base timer runs out holds at 0:00 briefly instead of disappearing — spell ranks lengthen mezzes, and your own casts teach EQBuddy the real duration (any rank, remembered permanently).

NEW: Mez chips — a small stack (💤) appears while anything is mesmerized, counting down to wake-up, and clears the moment something breaks it. It works from ANY group member's EQBuddy, not just the mez'er — the log tells everyone. Durations come from the wiki; your own casts teach it exact rank-corrected times. Drag it anywhere; it remembers.

Charmed pets now appear instantly for EVERY class. Charm landing lines turn out to differ by class — enchanter targets are 'charmed', druid/shaman animals 'blink', necro undead 'moan', and bard song targets' 'eyes glaze over' — and EQBuddy only knew two of the four. Thanks to Vellum670 for the complete charm list that cracked this.
Bard fix: song lines ('You begin to sing …') were never recognized, so bard charms and mezzes couldn't track at all. They do now.
Charm spells EQBuddy learns from your play are now remembered permanently instead of forgotten at restart.

Linux: the build now reports its real version (it claimed 1.26.0 forever and nagged itself to update — thanks to sahaq for the precise diagnosis), and update banners point at the Linux download instead of a Windows installer.

The Combat card's fight panel now shows the whole PULL — adds included. Multi-mob fights get a per-creature damage split, "Your damage" (your pet's rows finally included), and "Damage you took" with each hit or spell named by the creature that did it.

History gains a full "Encounters" review: every fight of the session as a collapsible row — who was fought, when, damage each way — expanding to the same full breakdown the live card shows. Recorded from this version forward.
An encounter is a pull, not a single creature: fights separated by less than 10 quiet seconds group together, in both the live card and History.
New High Contrast theme for tired eyes: solid background, pure white text — the see-through panels are what made other themes wash out over a bright game scene.

Or build your own: pick "Custom colors…" in Options and choose background, text, and accent (swatches or hex). EQBuddy fills in the rest and quietly fixes your text color if the combo would be unreadable.
The History window now graphs your DPS over time for each session (recorded from this version forward).
The DPS section shows damage by stance AND by invocation — invocations turned out to write a log line only when you change one, which is why this took until now.
Lost the widget after unplugging a monitor? Fixed: every window now checks its saved spot still exists on screen and comes back to a visible position if not.
Crushbone named run a measured 12:18 clock (was 9:00 — chips fired over 3 minutes early). Marrowbane, Chokehold, and Bloodgurgler were timed live to the second.
Pet damage tidies up: the Combat card's per-ability pet breakdown now collapses to one line — your pet's overall damage stays as its own row, and clicking "Pet abilities (N)" expands the split.

Charmed pets count from the very first hit: EQBuddy now claims your charm the instant the log says "X has been charmed." instead of waiting up to 9 seconds for the pet's first "Attacking… Master" tell. (Only YOUR charms — other players' charms nearby are correctly ignored.)

Spawn timers re-synced with the EQ Legends wiki, which is being actively corrected: Lower Guk now runs an 11-minute clock (was 28), Nektulos 6:00, Upper Guk 8:00, and Hadden is a 6-8 minute spawn, not 6 hours.
Named that were missing real timers got them: Equestrielle the Corrupted (60m, mist wolf placeholder), the Underbrush treants (~90s), Orc Chief (5m), Seahorse Matriarch (15m), Drelzna (18.5m).
22 more zones (mostly Kunark and the Planes) gained default respawn clocks — 109 of 119 zones now have one.
Remember: your own kills tighten any timer automatically, and anything you type in yourself always wins.
This popup! After each update, EQBuddy shows you what changed — once, and only the versions you actually skipped.
Weapon procs were already tracked (look for your proc's name, like Ignite, in Combat → Damage by attack) — now it's documented.
Buff and HoT fade alerts finally fire: EQBuddy now knows the wear-off flavor lines ('Your speed returns to normal.' is your haste dropping) even though the log never names the spell.
Spawn timers tighten themselves: re-kill a named sooner than its timer claimed and EQBuddy adopts the real gap. Your own typed values always win.
The Watch card leads with what just happened — 'last: Mesmerize (Gnoll elite) · 5m ago' — with the full list behind 'all N kinds'.
Plays nice with GINA and GamParse: log cleanup now stands down while they're running. If you use them regularly, also untick 'Auto-empty finished-session logs' in Options.
Every named can have its own respawn-due sound — Default is Alarm; pick per-row sounds to tell camps apart by ear (🔔 opts a camp in).
DUE chicklets tidy themselves away after a minute; click to dismiss sooner.
Spawn countdowns became chicklets: small movable chips, one per running timer, any zone. Double-click one for the full zone list.
Kill a named — or its placeholder — and the countdown starts from your log. 1,412 named across 119 zones ship built-in, and every duration is editable (your edits survive updates).
Spawn tracking follows you zone to zone, EQ Legends difficulty tiers ('Befallen 4 (Refined)') included.
Befallen's timers were rebuilt from real play data — most named there respawn in about four and a half minutes.
